chapters.title: Chapter 9: The Man Who Wanted Aurielle
paragraphs: "...He came to collect the loan."
The moment those words left the man’s mouth, I saw Aurielle’s expression stiffen slightly.
A trace of worry flashed through her purple eyes before she quietly let out a tired sigh and stood up from her chair.
The elderly maid immediately stepped forward and carefully placed a luxurious black robe over Aurielle’s shoulders.
Golden patterns shimmered faintly across the fabric under the sunlight.
Aurielle calmly adjusted her sleeves before turning toward the door.
But before she could leave—
"Aurielle."
She stopped mid-step and turned to look at me.
I took a small breath before asking,
"...Can I come with you?"
For a brief moment, surprise appeared on her face.
As if she hadn’t expected me to say that.
Then her eyes softened slightly before she looked away and nodded once.
"...Fine."
A small smile appeared on my face and I quickly followed after her.
The moment Aurielle stepped outside the room—
Her footsteps suddenly paused.
Her gaze landed directly on the ten female mages standing neatly in the hallway with staffs in their hands.
The corridor lamps reflected softly against their colorful robes and beautiful faces.
Even the servants nearby had secretly stopped working just to stare at them.
Aurielle blinked once.
Then slowly turned toward me.
"...Why are they all female?"
I froze for a second.
Out of everything, THAT was her first question?
She didn’t even seem surprised that they were mages.
Before I could explain further, she simply shook her head lightly and looked toward the elderly maid.
"Prepare rooms for them."
"Yes, Lady Aurielle."
The old maid bowed politely before guiding the confused mages away.
Meanwhile, I was still stunned by Aurielle’s earlier question.
"...Why does she care more about them being women than them being mages?"
I muttered internally.
Then I quickly snapped out of my thoughts after seeing Aurielle already walking away.
I hurried after her through the corridor.
The mansion hallways were quiet.
Soft orange lights flickered from the wall lamps while servants lowered their heads respectfully as Aurielle passed.
Outside the windows, the dark mountains surrounding Blackstone Highlands could barely be seen beneath the cloudy morning sky.
"Aurielle..."
I lowered my voice slightly after catching up beside her.
"They are gifts from the Goddess of Luck."
"...So it’s not my fault."
Aurielle glanced sideways at me.
Then her lips twitched slightly.
She muttered something under her breath so quietly I almost couldn’t hear it.
"...So now you’re cheating on the Goddess of Light too."
"...What?"
"Nothing."
She calmly continued walking.
Meanwhile, I stood there for half a second with an ugly expression.
"...Why do I feel like I’m being judged for crimes I didn’t commit?"
Soon, after walking for around a minute, we finally arrived in front of the guest reception hall.
Two guards standing outside immediately straightened their backs and opened the large doors.
CREEEAK—
The moment we entered, warm air mixed with the smell of expensive perfume drifted toward us.
Inside, a fat middle-aged man sat comfortably on a luxurious sofa while drinking wine.
Baron Cedric Thornvale.
He wore an extravagant dark-red noble robe lined with gold embroidery, and almost every finger carried expensive rings.
On both sides of him sat two young beautiful women dressed in revealing silk clothes.
Their outfits exposed deep lines from their necks down to their waists while thin fabric barely covered the rest.
My eyes instinctively drifted toward them for half a second.
Then—
OUCH!
A sharp pain suddenly exploded from my waist.
I nearly jumped.
I turned immediately toward Aurielle.
She was smiling calmly.
But her purple eyes were giving me a death glare.
"...I wasn’t even staring that hard."
I muttered weakly.
Her glare only became colder.
I immediately shut my mouth.
Meanwhile, Cedric’s gaze slowly moved toward us.
The moment his eyes landed on me—
Disgust appeared openly across his face.
But then his eyes shifted toward Aurielle.
And my expression darkened instantly.
Because the way he looked at her was filthy.
His eyes slowly scanned her body from top to bottom while a lecherous grin spread across his lips.
He even licked his lips slightly.
My blood pressure instantly rose.
A faint golden glow flickered across my arm.
But before I could step forward—
A soft hand suddenly grabbed mine.
"...No need."
Aurielle’s quiet voice entered my ears.
I turned toward her and saw her expression remained calm.
But her fingers gripping my hand were slightly tight.
Clearly—
She was angry too.
I slowly took a deep breath and suppressed the pressure leaking from my body.
Soon both of us sat opposite Cedric.
Cedric spread his arms with a fake warm smile.
"Baroness Aurielle Valmont..."
"I’m truly happy to see you again after such a long time."
Despite speaking politely, his hands were still resting shamelessly on the thighs of the women beside him.
Aurielle’s expression didn’t change.
"Greetings, Baron Cedric Thornvale."
Her cold voice echoed calmly throughout the room.
"Can you explain why you came here so suddenly?"
"I’m quite busy."
"...Nice reply, wifey."
I thought proudly while sitting beside her.
Cedric’s smile twitched slightly after hearing her cold tone.
Then he sighed dramatically.
"You know, Miss Aurielle..."
"...ten years ago your mother, Lady Seraphina, borrowed a very large amount of gold from me to maintain this territory."
The moment her mother’s name was mentioned—
A shadow briefly crossed Aurielle’s eyes.
But she quickly hid it.
"I already paid this year’s interest."
"Then why are you here?"
Cedric gave another fake helpless sigh.
"I know that."
"But recently my finances have become somewhat... tight."
He leaned slightly forward.
"So I’ve started collecting debts from various places."
Then a cunning smile slowly appeared on his face.
"That is why..."
"...I now require the FULL repayment amount, Miss Aurielle."
Aurielle’s expression stiffened slightly.
But before she could respond—
Cedric continued speaking.
"Of course..."
"I understand your situation."
"You were exiled."
"You lost your support."
"And this territory is barely surviving."
A large smile spread across his face.
"So how about this?"
"You sell Blackstone Highlands to me."
"I’ll forgive the debt..."
"...and even generously return the remaining value afterward."
I saw Aurielle’s fingers tighten beneath the table.
But Cedric wasn’t finished.
His eyes slowly scanned her body again.
"If you truly wish to keep the territory..."
His smile became disgusting.
"You could simply become my wife."
"And naturally..."
"...all debts would disappear."
BOOM—
A heavy pressure exploded from my body instantly.
Golden lines faintly appeared across my arms.
The room temperature dropped slightly.
The two women beside Cedric immediately turned pale.
Even the wine inside Cedric’s glass trembled.
But Cedric himself remained calm.
Slowly—
He turned his gaze toward me.
"Mister Luke."
Our eyes met.
"You should control your murderous aura."
"I understand you are unfamiliar with noble laws..."
His eyes slowly drifted toward my simple linen clothes.
Then disgust appeared across his face again.
"But attacking a noble is one of the greatest crimes within the empire."
"You would be hunted down by the entire empire."
Then he paused intentionally before glancing toward Aurielle.
"...Alongside everyone connected to you."
The moment those words fell—
Aurielle quietly grabbed my hand again.
I looked toward her.
Her face remained calm.
But I could see her gritting her teeth slightly.
I slowly took a deep breath before speaking in a cold voice.
"...How much?"
Cedric blinked once.
Clearly confused.
So I repeated myself.
"How much is the total debt?"
Cedric stared at me for a second before laughing mockingly.
"I doubt you’ve ever even seen that amount of money before..."
"...but it’s six hundred gold coins."
He casually placed several papers onto the table.
The documents carried both his seal and Lady Seraphina’s seal.
My expression changed slightly.
Then I turned toward Aurielle.
"How much was the original amount?"
Aurielle looked confused by my question but still answered.
"...One hundred gold coins."
I nodded slowly.
"...Fifty gold interest every year."
"What a disgusting bastard."
I muttered internally.
Then—
FLASH.
Six heavy gold pouches suddenly appeared on the table one after another.
CLANK.
CLANK.
CLANK.
The sound of gold echoed heavily throughout the room.
Cedric froze instantly.
Aurielle’s eyes widened slightly.
Even the servants nearby stared in shock.
I calmly leaned back before speaking loudly.
"Six hundred gold coins."
"From this moment onward..."
"...Baroness Aurielle Valmont no longer owes any debt to Baron Cedric Thornvale."
For a few seconds—
Cedric simply stared at the gold silently.
Then toward the contract papers.
Then toward Aurielle.
His face slowly became uglier and uglier.
Because this situation had completely escaped his control.
Still—
He eventually grabbed the gold pouches.
After all, six hundred gold coins was still a massive amount for him.
But just as he was about to stand up—
"Mister Baron."
Cedric paused and slowly turned toward me.
My face was calm.
But my voice turned cold.
"...My money is not easy to digest."
For a brief second, Cedric’s expression stiffened slightly.
Then a mocking smile slowly appeared on his lips.
"...What can a talentless Hero even do?"
He muttered quietly under his breath.
But I still heard it clearly.
Soon he stood up and left alongside the two women.
CREEEAK—
The large doors closed behind him.
Silence filled the room instantly.
Then suddenly—
"Luke."
I turned around.
Aurielle was staring directly at me now.
Her purple eyes were filled with disbelief.
"What was THAT?"
"Where did you get so much money?"
"And why didn’t you tell me anything?"
One question came after another rapidly.
I smiled helplessly before gently holding her hand.
That finally made her stop talking.
"I told you already."
"The Goddess of Luck gave me gifts."
Aurielle stared at me suspiciously for several seconds.
Then eventually sighed.
"...Fine."
"Don’t tell me."
I awkwardly scratched my cheek while smiling.
But then—
Aurielle’s eyes slowly narrowed.
"And now..."
"...who exactly are those ten women?"
She asked while giving me another terrifying death glare.
"...Gulp."
[Chapter End]

But then his eyes shifted toward Aurielle.
And my expression darkened instantly.
Because the way he looked at her was filthy.
His eyes slowly scanned her body from top to bottom while a lecherous grin spread across his lips.
He even licked his lips slightly.
My blood pressure instantly rose.
A faint golden glow flickered across my arm.
But before I could step forward—
A soft hand suddenly grabbed mine.
"...No need."
Aurielle’s quiet voice entered my ears.
I turned toward her and saw her expression remained calm.
But her fingers gripping my hand were slightly tight.
Clearly—
She was angry too.
I slowly took a deep breath and suppressed the pressure leaking from my body.
Soon both of us sat opposite Cedric.
Cedric spread his arms with a fake warm smile.
"Baroness Aurielle Valmont..."
"I’m truly happy to see you again after such a long time."
Despite speaking politely, his hands were still resting shamelessly on the thighs of the women beside him.
Aurielle’s expression didn’t change.
"Greetings, Baron Cedric Thornvale."
Her cold voice echoed calmly throughout the room.
"Can you explain why you came here so suddenly?"
"I’m quite busy."
"...Nice reply, wifey."
I thought proudly while sitting beside her.
Cedric’s smile twitched slightly after hearing her cold tone.
Then he sighed dramatically.
"You know, Miss Aurielle..."
"...ten years ago your mother, Lady Seraphina, borrowed a very large amount of gold from me to maintain this territory."
The moment her mother’s name was mentioned—
A shadow briefly crossed Aurielle’s eyes.
But she quickly hid it.
"I already paid this year’s interest."
"Then why are you here?"
Cedric gave another fake helpless sigh.
"I know that."
"But recently my finances have become somewhat... tight."
He leaned slightly forward.
"So I’ve started collecting debts from various places."
Then a cunning smile slowly appeared on his face.
"That is why..."
"...I now require the FULL repayment amount, Miss Aurielle."
Aurielle’s expression stiffened slightly.
But before she could respond—
Cedric continued speaking.
"Of course..."
"I understand your situation."
"You were exiled."
"You lost your support."
"And this territory is barely surviving."
A large smile spread across his face.
"So how about this?"
"You sell Blackstone Highlands to me."
"I’ll forgive the debt..."
"...and even generously return the remaining value afterward."
I saw Aurielle’s fingers tighten beneath the table.
But Cedric wasn’t finished.
His eyes slowly scanned her body again.
"If you truly wish to keep the territory..."
His smile became disgusting.
"You could simply become my wife."
"And naturally..."
"...all debts would disappear."
BOOM—
A heavy pressure exploded from my body instantly.
Golden lines faintly appeared across my arms.
The room temperature dropped slightly.
The two women beside Cedric immediately turned pale.
Even the wine inside Cedric’s glass trembled.
But Cedric himself remained calm.
Slowly—
He turned his gaze toward me.
"Mister Luke."
Our eyes met.
"You should control your murderous aura."
"I understand you are unfamiliar with noble laws..."
His eyes slowly drifted toward my simple linen clothes.
Then disgust appeared across his face again.
"But attacking a noble is one of the greatest crimes within the empire."
"You would be hunted down by the entire empire."
Then he paused intentionally before glancing toward Aurielle.
"...Alongside everyone connected to you."
The moment those words fell—
Aurielle quietly grabbed my hand again.
I looked toward her.
Her face remained calm.
But I could see her gritting her teeth slightly.
I slowly took a deep breath before speaking in a cold voice.
"...How much?"
Cedric blinked once.
Clearly confused.
So I repeated myself.
"How much is the total debt?"
Cedric stared at me for a second before laughing mockingly.
"I doubt you’ve ever even seen that amount of money before..."
"...but it’s six hundred gold coins."
He casually placed several papers onto the table.
The documents carried both his seal and Lady Seraphina’s seal.
My expression changed slightly.
Then I turned toward Aurielle.
"How much was the original amount?"
Aurielle looked confused by my question but still answered.
"...One hundred gold coins."
I nodded slowly.
"...Fifty gold interest every year."
"What a disgusting bastard."
I muttered internally.
Then—
FLASH.
Six heavy gold pouches suddenly appeared on the table one after another.
CLANK.
CLANK.
CLANK.
The sound of gold echoed heavily throughout the room.
Cedric froze instantly.
Aurielle’s eyes widened slightly.
Even the servants nearby stared in shock.
I calmly leaned back before speaking loudly.
"Six hundred gold coins."
"From this moment onward..."
"...Baroness Aurielle Valmont no longer owes any debt to Baron Cedric Thornvale."
For a few seconds—
Cedric simply stared at the gold silently.
Then toward the contract papers.
Then toward Aurielle.
His face slowly became uglier and uglier.
Because this situation had completely escaped his control.
Still—
He eventually grabbed the gold pouches.
After all, six hundred gold coins was still a massive amount for him.
But just as he was about to stand up—
"Mister Baron."
Cedric paused and slowly turned toward me.
My face was calm.
But my voice turned cold.
"...My money is not easy to digest."
For a brief second, Cedric’s expression stiffened slightly.
Then a mocking smile slowly appeared on his lips.
"...What can a talentless Hero even do?"
He muttered quietly under his breath.
But I still heard it clearly.
Soon he stood up and left alongside the two women.
CREEEAK—
The large doors closed behind him.
Silence filled the room instantly.
Then suddenly—
"Luke."
I turned around.
Aurielle was staring directly at me now.
Her purple eyes were filled with disbelief.
"What was THAT?"
"Where did you get so much money?"
"And why didn’t you tell me anything?"
One question came after another rapidly.
I smiled helplessly before gently holding her hand.
That finally made her stop talking.
"I told you already."
"The Goddess of Luck gave me gifts."
Aurielle stared at me suspiciously for several seconds.
Then eventually sighed.
"...Fine."
"Don’t tell me."
I awkwardly scratched my cheek while smiling.
But then—
Aurielle’s eyes slowly narrowed.
"And now..."
"...who exactly are those ten women?"
She asked while giving me another terrifying death glare.
"...Gulp."
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Light of Hope
paragraphs: I hurriedly explained to Aurielle that the ten women were Apprentice Mages and even told her about their different elemental affinities.
But after hearing everything—
She only reacted to one word.
"...Light Mage?"
Her purple eyes widened slightly.
I got confused by her sudden reaction, but still nodded slowly.
The next moment—
She grabbed my wrist tightly and hurriedly dragged me out of the room.
"W-Wait—"
I barely had time to react before she started walking quickly through the mansion corridors toward the mages’ resting room.
Her footsteps echoed rapidly against the stone floor.
Clearly—
She was desperate.
BANG!
The door suddenly burst open as we entered.
The female mages jumped in shock because they were already nervous in an unfamiliar mansion.
"M-Master!"
But the moment they saw me, their tense expressions relaxed immediately.
They respectfully bowed toward both me and Aurielle.
However—
Aurielle’s gaze wasn’t on them.
It was on me.
I immediately understood what she wanted.
"...Elena."
The moment my words fell, all the mages turned toward one girl.
A beautiful young woman with long blonde hair, soft golden eyes, and fair skin slowly stepped forward.
"Master."
Elena approached quietly before kneeling respectfully in front of me.
And unfortunately—
The moment she moved, even her loose robes failed to hide her overwhelming figure.
My eyes almost drifted downward instinctively.
*Cough.*
I quickly coughed to hide my embarrassment.
Thankfully Aurielle wasn’t paying attention to me right now.
Her eyes were completely locked onto Elena.
Almost immediately, Aurielle stepped forward and sat down in front of her before tightly holding Elena’s hands.
"Can you use healing magic?"
Her voice carried obvious urgency.
Like this answer alone could solve countless problems.
Elena became slightly embarrassed by the sudden closeness but still nodded softly.
"I can."
The moment those words left her mouth—
Aurielle’s face brightened instantly.
"Perfect..."
Then suddenly—
She hugged Elena tightly.
My eyes widened.
Because from where I stood—
The sight was honestly dangerous to my mental health.
Because both of their assest are tightly pressing hard against each other.
"Gulp."
The swallowing sound escaped before I could stop it.
Aurielle immediately froze.
Then slowly turned toward me.
Her beautiful face became slightly red after realizing what position she was in.
She quickly stood up and cleared her throat.
"T-Thank you, Luke."
"The territory has many sick people..."
"Some are even infected with demonic miasma."
Her grateful voice became softer near the end.
I smiled after hearing that.
"It’s fine."
I lightly hit my chest proudly.
"You don’t need to worry anymore."
"Because I’m your husband."
"And your problems are my problems too."
The moment I said those words—
Aurielle’s face reddened slightly again.
"Hmph."
She turned her face away immediately before walking toward the exit.
But I still noticed the faint smile trying to appear on her lips.
Soon we left the mansion together.
The afternoon sun illuminated the high stone walls of Blackstone Highlands while cold mountain winds blew through the fortress city.
The moment we crossed the mansion gates, I noticed guards wearing heavy plate armor patrolling the area.
Large travel carriages stood nearby while merchants prepared supplies for mountain journeys.
The guards immediately saluted Aurielle respectfully whenever they saw her.
However—
One man didn’t.
A tall muscular knight wearing black armor leaned lazily against the wall while staring openly at Aurielle’s body.
The vice captain.
A smirk slowly spread across his face.
"Lady Aurielle..."
"You look even more beautiful today."
His tone carried zero respect.
And he didn’t even bother looking at me.
Aurielle’s expression instantly turned cold.
"Do your job."
Her voice cut through the air sharply.
Then she continued walking without stopping.
Behind us, the vice captain’s expression became ugly.
But his gaze still remained fixed shamelessly on her figure.
"My Lord..."
"Why not just claim her already?"
One nearby soldier asked curiously.
The vice captain laughed quietly.
"Taming a lioness is far more enjoyable than handling some obedient cow."
"Hahaha!"
Several soldiers burst into laughter together.
The sound echoed behind us.
My fists clenched instantly.
A faint golden glow almost appeared around my arm.
But suddenly—
Aurielle grabbed my wrist tightly.
"Don’t."
Her voice became serious.
"He’s at the Peak Bronze Knight Realm."
"Same realm as Lucien... except far stronger."
She looked directly into my eyes.
"So don’t provoke him."
My expression darkened.
"I don’t like the way he looks at you."
The moment those words left my mouth—
Aurielle’s expression softened slightly.
For just a brief second—
A strange warmth appeared inside her heart.
Something she hadn’t felt in a very long time.
A faint smile appeared on her lips.
But before she could say anything—
"Master, don’t worry!"
Elena suddenly spoke confidently from beside us.
"You are supreme."
"You’ll definitely beat that bastard one day."
Her golden eyes were practically shining with fanatic admiration.
My expression froze instantly.
Meanwhile Aurielle slowly turned toward us with a weird look.
Then silently continued walking.
After passing through the inner fortress gate, we finally entered the civilian district.
And immediately—
The atmosphere changed completely.
The streets became dirtier.
The stone roads were cracked.
Several buildings looked damaged and poorly maintained.
Many houses had broken roofs patched together with old wood and cloth.
The smell of smoke, sweat, cheap food, and damp air mixed together heavily.
People walked silently through the streets with exhausted expressions.
Thin children sat quietly near alleyways.
Old workers dragged tired bodies through the roads.
Some merchants still operated small stalls, but their faces lacked energy.
Many travelers and merchant groups passed through the territory with hired mercenaries because crossing Blackstone Highlands was still the fastest route through the mountains.
Dangerous—
But much cheaper than circling around the mountain ranges for weeks.
Yet despite the crowded roads—
Almost nobody paid attention to Aurielle.
Not because they hated her.
But because most people here had already lost hope long ago.
They looked too tired to care anymore.
I quietly glanced toward Aurielle.
And for the first time—
I understood how heavy the burden on her shoulders really was.
Soon we finally arrived at the clinic.
The building itself looked old and worn down.
Wooden boards creaked beneath our feet as we entered.
The moment I stepped inside—
The strong smell of herbs and medicine filled my nose.
Several injured patients lay weakly on beds while others leaned against the walls coughing painfully.
Some even had black marks spreading across their skin from demonic miasma infection.
Near the front table stood an elderly man with messy gray hair, a long white beard, and tired deep-brown eyes hidden behind small round glasses.
He wore old dark healer robes covered with faint herb stains while carefully mixing medicine inside a small bowl.
Doctor Aldric Vayne.
Beside him worked a young woman with chestnut-brown hair tied into a loose ponytail and soft hazel eyes.
She wore cream-colored healer clothes lightly stained with herbs while small medicinal pouches hung around her waist.
Clara Fenwood.
Meanwhile nearby—
A short black-haired girl with amber eyes and lightly tanned skin hurried between patients while changing bandages quickly.
Rolled-up sleeves exposed her hardworking arms while a dark apron covered her simple clothes.
Yuna Bell.
"Doctor Aldric."
The old man paused immediately after hearing Aurielle’s voice.
Then both he and his assistants turned around in surprise.
"Aurielle..."
"You finally returned."
A warm smile appeared on his tired face.
Even Mira smiled gently.
Several injured patients also noticed Aurielle and tried to kneel weakly.
But she quickly raised he
"There’s no need."
Her voice remained calm and gentle.
Seeing this scene—
I quietly realized something.
Even after years of suffering...
These people still trusted their new lord.
Aurielle then guided Elena toward a heavily injured young man lying on one of the beds.
An arrow had pierced near his lungs.
His breathing sounded painful and unstable.
"Elena..."
"See if you can heal him."
Aurielle spoke softly.
Elena nodded immediately.
Then she turned toward me.
"Master... please remove the arrow when I signal."
I nodded.
Soon everyone nearby gathered around curiously.
Even Doctor Aldric approached carefully alongside his assistants.
Because healing magic—
Especially Light Healing Magic—
Was practically legendary in a remote border territory like this.
I tightly grabbed the arrow.
Then—
When Elena nodded—
I pulled it out instantly.
"AAAHHHHH!"
The young man screamed painfully.
Blood spilled from the wound immediately.
But Elena calmly raised her staff.
"Healing Wounds."
Warm golden light bloomed throughout the clinic.
The bleeding slowly stopped.
Then the wound visibly began closing.
Everyone gasped loudly.
Some patients even stood up in disbelief.
"Healing magic..."
"It’s real..."
Doctor Aldric himself looked stunned.
But Elena continued casting one spell after another.
"Healing Wounds."
"Fatigue Recovery."
"Light Purification."
Soft holy light repeatedly filled the clinic.
The dark miasma marks slowly disappeared from infected patients.
Their pale faces gradually regained color.
Even the atmosphere inside the building changed completely.
Finally—
The young man stood up shakily.
Then touched his healed chest in disbelief.
"I... I’m healed?"
"There’s no pain anymore!"
"Hahaha!"
Tears filled his eyes as he laughed loudly.
Soon everyone looked toward Elena with reverence.
That was when I suddenly stepped forward and spoke loudly.
"You should all thank your Baroness."
"She spent enormous resources to recruit a Light Mage for this territory."
The moment those words echoed—
Everyone turned toward Aurielle.
She stared at me with a completely baffled expression.
Then—
"Long live the Baroness!"
"Long live Lady Aurielle!"
"Long live the Baroness!"
Voices suddenly echoed throughout the clinic.
Even merchants and travelers outside began peeking inside curiously.
Meanwhile—
Aurielle stood frozen slightly.
Because perhaps...
This was the first time in a long while someone openly praised her efforts.
By the time Elena finished healing patients one after another—
The sun had already started setting.
Orange evening light entered through the clinic windows while exhaustion covered Elena’s face.
She repeatedly sat down to recover mana before continuing again.
But in the end—
Every patient left the clinic smiling.
Healthy.
Hopeful.
Some even tried leaving small payments behind.
But Aurielle refused all of them quietly.
Eventually we prepared to leave.
"We should return now."
Aurielle spoke softly toward Doctor Aldric.
The old healer nodded alongside his assistants.
But then—
I looked toward Elena.
She had completely exhausted herself and fallen asleep on a nearby couch while still holding her staff loosely.
I walked toward her intending to carry her.
But suddenly—
SLAP.
Aurielle smacked my hand away.
Then before I could react—
She carefully lifted Elena onto her back herself.
"You’re married."
"So stop touching other women carelessly."
Her voice sounded strangely annoyed.
Behind us, Mira and Celestine tried hiding their laughter while even Doctor Aldric showed a small amused smile.
Then suddenly—
Doctor Aldric looked directly at me.
"Take care of Aurielle."
"She has already suffered far too much."
His tired voice carried genuine concern.
I smiled softly before nodding seriously.
"I will."
Then I quickly hurried after Aurielle.
By the time we returned to the mansion—
Night had already fallen.
Moonlight illuminated the dark fortress walls while cold mountain winds blew across Blackstone Highlands.
The servants quietly lit lanterns throughout the mansion hallways.
Eventually—
After dinner and several more discussions—
I finally returned toward my room.
But after few moment later the door opened.—
My mind froze completely.
"...Why are we sleeping in the same room?"
Standing near the entrance was a breathtaking woman with raven-black hair and deep purple eyes.
Soft moonlight poured through the window and illuminated her beautiful face.
She wore a loose violet nightgown that barely hid her graceful figure.
And unfortunately—
Something deep inside me instantly woke up after remembering the night with Selene.
"...Gulp."
[Chapter End]
And finally—
Chapter 10 is here.
Thank you everyone, and more Chapters are coming soon.

Their discipline was different.
At the front stood several powerful figures.
Three Bronze Knights.
Alongside them—
Vice Captain.

My expression darkened.
Something felt wrong.
Very wrong.

"Sir?"

"Why are there so many soldiers without our territory’s insignia?"

Five hundred outside soldiers.
Three Bronze Knights.
A territory whose defenses were already stretched thin.

Somebody was planning something.

He was involved.

"Something is definitely about to happen."

chapters.title: Chapter 14: The Wells of Hope
paragraphs: "I will discuss this problem with Aurielle after returning."
I gave the soldiers one last look before turning and walking away.
The moment Luke crossed the gate of the lord’s mansion, Roland Ashenford, who had been laughing with several Bronze Knights, suddenly paused.
His smile slowly disappeared.
His fingers tapped lightly against the hilt of his sword.
Then his gaze landed on Luke’s departing figure.
A dangerous glint appeared in his eyes.
"Go."
His voice was calm.
The nearby Bronze Knights immediately stopped talking.
Roland’s lips curled into a cold smile.
"That bastard dared to touch my lioness."
"Break both his hands."
He paused.
Then his smile widened.
"And make sure to castrate him so, he never able to drink about any woman again."
Five Iron Knights immediately stepped forward and bowed.
"As you command, Young Master."
Without hesitation, they quietly followed after Luke.
One of the Bronze Knights frowned.
"Is this really alright?"
Roland merely chuckled.
"It will be."
His eyes remained fixed on Luke’s back.
"You will know soon enough."
He said nothing more.
Soon the group returned to discussing women and drinking as though nothing had happened.
The moment I left the lord’s mansion grounds, that familiar foul smell entered my nose again.
I frowned but endured it.
Then I began observing the territory carefully.
The deeper I walked into Blackstone Highlands, the heavier my mood became.
The roads were cracked.
Several houses had damaged roofs patched together using old wooden boards.
Children ran barefoot through muddy streets.
Some adults looked exhausted despite it still being midday.
Yet what surprised me most wasn’t the poverty.
It was the silence.
Nobody complained.
Nobody protested.
They simply endured.
As though suffering had become normal.
After several hours of walking and asking questions, I discovered something surprising.
Despite being poor, Blackstone Highlands possessed quite a few important facilities.
Blacksmith shops.
Alchemy stores.
Merchant associations.
Adventurer Guilds.
Mercenary Guilds.
At first, I couldn’t understand why.
This territory looked nearly bankrupt.
But after asking around, I finally learned the reason.
Blackstone Highlands connected directly to the Ashveil Trade Route.
One of the major roads connecting frontier territories and nearby kingdoms.
Although dangerous due to monsters and bandits, merchants still traveled through it constantly.
Why?
Because crossing through Blackstone Highlands reduced travel time by weeks compared to going around the mountains.
But that wasn’t the only reason.
"Stormhowl Mountains."
I looked toward the massive mountain range visible in the distance.
Towering peaks stretched endlessly toward the clouds.
Ancient forests covered their slopes.
Powerful monster roars occasionally echoed from deep within.
The mountains acted like a natural wall that prevented demon armies from easily advancing into nearby territories.
At the same time, they contained countless resources.
Monster materials.
Medicinal herbs.
Rare ores.
Hidden caves.
Ancient ruins.
Naturally, adventurers and traders were drawn here like moths to a flame.
"Aurielle is literally sitting on a gold mine."
I muttered.
Unfortunately, she didn’t seem to have the manpower needed to properly exploit it.
As I continued walking toward the farming district, I suddenly spotted a familiar face.
The black-haired young man who had delivered Aurielle’s message before.
"Hello."
I greeted him.
The young man immediately stopped.
The moment he recognized me, his posture straightened.
"Young Master."
He bowed respectfully.
Only then did I realize something.
I had never asked for his name.
"What’s your name?"
"Noah, Young Master."
He replied politely.
Noah was an orphan taken in years ago by Lady Isabella Valmont, Aurielle’s mother.
Since then, he had grown up inside the manor and become one of the most trusted attendants of the household.
I nodded.
Then immediately asked about the territory’s water situation.
The moment I brought up the topic, Noah’s expression darkened.
"Young Master..."
"The main water source comes from a river in the east."
He paused.
Then clenched his fists.
"But Baron Cedric’s territory is located upstream."
A trace of anger appeared in his eyes.
"He often blocks the river using dams."
"Sometimes..."
His voice trembled slightly.
"He pollutes it as well."
My expression darkened.
Noah lowered his head.
"Last winter, dozens of villagers became sick."
"Three children died after drinking contaminated water."
His fists tightened.
"But nobody could do anything."
"Lady Aurielle sent complaints several times."
"He ignored all of them."
Silence followed.
The more I listened, the worse my mood became.
"What about wells and ponds?"
I finally asked.
Noah nodded.

Golden mana erupted around my body.
The First Form of Titan Knight activated.
A heavy aura burst outward.

The ground cracked beneath my feet.
The villagers stared in shock.

My body disappeared.

THUD!!

Their eyes looked empty.
Hopeless.
Like people who had suffered for far too long.

Tears appeared in her eyes.
"Free...?"
Her voice trembled.

Hundreds of villagers followed behind us.
Some children even ran ahead while shouting excitedly.

The signs of poverty were obvious everywhere.

Noah explained quietly.

Noah said sadly.

I nodded.

Clean water.

Then another.
Then another.

Then another.
Then another.

Some cried.
Some smiled.
Some simply stared at the flowing water as if afraid it would disappear.

"Thank you!"
"Thank you!"
Their voices echoed throughout the district.

Then raised my hand.
"If you want to thank someone..."

"She’s the one who brought me here."
The crowd froze.
Then—

"LONG LIVE LADY AURIELLE!!"
The cheers shook the entire district.

She deserved this.

THUD.

I looked toward the farmers.

The villagers froze.
Noah’s eyes widened.
And for the first time in years—
Hope truly returned to Blackstone Highlands.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: The First Chain Breaks
paragraphs: "Let’s solve the food problem too."
With that, I began distributing the Mana Wheat Seeds.
The moment the bags opened, the villagers crowded around in excitement.
Within minutes, all ten bags had been distributed.
"Good."
A satisfied smile appeared on my face.
I raised one of the remaining seeds and spoke loudly enough for everyone to hear.
"These aren’t ordinary wheat seeds."
The crowd immediately became attentive.
"I specifically brought these here."
"This wheat grows nearly ten times faster than normal crops."
"It also requires very little water and maintenance."
The moment those words left my mouth—
The entire crowd froze.
Their eyes widened.
Several farmers looked at the seeds in their hands as though they were holding treasure.
Because they understood exactly what this meant.
Normally, they would spend months waiting for a harvest.
Months of hard labor.
Months of uncertainty.
Months of praying that droughts, monsters, or bad weather wouldn’t destroy everything.
But now...
They could harvest far sooner.
Food shortages could finally ease.
For many families, this meant survival.
"Thank you, Sir!"
A middle-aged farmer suddenly shouted.
Soon others joined.
"Thank you!"
"Thank you, Young Master!"
"We’ll never forget this!"
I smiled and waved my hand.
Then I instructed Noah to organize the seed distribution and make sure everyone planted them today.
Noah nodded enthusiastically.
"I’ll take care of it, Young Master."
After everything was settled, I finally left the village alone and started walking back toward the mansion.
The sun had already begun setting.
Golden light stretched across the fields.
A cool breeze rustled the grass.
For a brief moment, everything felt peaceful.
Then—
Crunch.
A branch snapped.
I stopped walking.
My eyes narrowed.
Several armored figures stepped out from behind nearby trees.
Others casually emerged from the shadows.
Five men.
All wearing steel knight armor.
Their armor bore traces of long service.
Numerous scratches.
Dried blood stains.
Battle-worn capes.
Most importantly—
Every one of them radiated the aura of a Peak Iron Knight.
One of them smirked.
"Took you long enough, Young Master."
He paused before mocking laughter escaped his mouth.
"Or should I say..."
"Talentless Hero."
"Hahahahaha!"
The other four immediately burst into laughter.
I remained silent.
My eyes carefully observed each of them.
Professional soldiers.
Not bandits.
Not mercenaries.
These men had killed before.
A lot.
"Who sent you?"
I asked calmly.
The leader grinned and said something.
"You touched something that belongs to our lord."
His expression gradually became colder.
"The Baroness."
"Our lord has wanted her for years."
He slowly drew his sword.
CLING.
The blade reflected the evening sunlight.
"Now he wants your hands."
He pointed the sword toward me.
"And your manhood."
The others began surrounding me.
Like wolves cornering prey.
"Take your punishment."
BOOM!
Golden energy erupted from my body.
Titan Physique activated.
The ground beneath my feet cracked.
The five knights’ expressions changed slightly.
Then the leader charged.
BANG!
My fist slammed directly into his chest armor.
The steel immediately bent inward.
CRASH!
His body shot backward like a cannonball and smashed into the ground.
But before I could capitalize—
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The remaining four attacked simultaneously.
Their coordination was excellent.
One targeted my head.
One my legs.
One my back.
One aimed directly for my heart.
CLANG!
I caught a sword with my bare hand.
Blood immediately appeared.
The blade cut through my skin despite the golden energy coating it.
"Damn."
BANG!
I punched the attacker across the jaw.
His helmet dented inward.
But another sword immediately slashed across my back.
SLASH!
Pain exploded through my body.
Blood sprayed.
A third knight stabbed toward my shoulder.
PHUCH!
The blade pierced flesh.
I gritted my teeth.
These weren’t weak opponents.
They were experienced Iron Knights attacking together.
BAM!
I kicked one away.
CRASH!
He smashed into a tree.
But moments later he stood again.
Injured.
Yet still fighting.
The first knight I had punched also staggered back to his feet.
Blood dripped from his mouth.
Yet his eyes remained vicious.
Five against one.
And they knew exactly how to work together.
"This is bad."
I dodged another thrust.
A sword barely missed my throat.
The tip sliced my cheek.
Blood trickled down.
Another attack came immediately after.
No openings.
No hesitation.
Only relentless pressure.
Then—
The System’s voice echoed.
[Luke.]
[You have reached Body Tempering Realm.]
[Second Form Available.]
[Summon the first armour.]
[Do it quickly.]
For the first time—
I heard urgency in the System’s voice.
I didn’t hesitate.
I raised my hand.
The surrounding world suddenly became silent.
"From the forgotten Void beyond time..."
The five knights paused.
The air itself felt wrong.
"Heed my command..."
Darkness spread.
Not physical darkness.
Something deeper.
Older.
A darkness that existed before light.
"Velzareth..."
Far above.
Beyond mortal sight.
Ancient beings sleeping in forgotten dimensions slowly opened their eyes.
Ancient gods paused.
Primordial entities looked toward the mortal world.
Something they had not seen for countless ages...
Had awakened.
"Warden of the Void Path."
The world froze.
For a fraction of a second—
Reality itself seemed to stop breathing.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
Void energy erupted.
The sky darkened.
Azure-blue runes illuminated the surroundings.
The five knights instantly fell to one knee.
Their faces filled with terror.
"What... what is this?!"
The leader shouted.
Then it appeared.
Inside an endless black void behind me—
A suit of ancient armor floated silently.
Velzareth.
Matte black armor.
Azure-blue runes flowing across its surface like living veins.
A dark cape swayed gently despite the complete absence of wind.
The armor radiated neither holiness nor malice.
Neither light nor darkness.
Only inevitability.
Like a silent executioner that had waited countless ages for its master to return.
CLINK.
CLINK.
CLINK.
The sound of chains echoed through the battlefield.
Then—
Twelve enormous Void Chains materialized around my body.
Each chain stretched endlessly into the surrounding Void, disappearing into unseen depths beyond reality itself.
Ancient.
Heavy.
Oppressive.
Like restraints forged to bind something that should never have existed.
The sight alone caused the surrounding Iron Knights to instinctively step back.
Among the twelve chains, only a single chain was connected to Velzareth.
The remaining eleven vanished into the endless darkness beyond the Void.
No one knew what lay at their other ends.
No one could see it.
Yet merely looking at those chains filled the heart with an indescribable sense of dread.
As if unimaginably terrifying beings slumbered beyond them.
As if Velzareth was only the first thing being restrained.
Then—
CRACK.
The chain connected to Velzareth shattered.
The sound echoed like a divine decree across heaven and earth.
For a brief moment, the remaining eleven chains rattled violently.
As though something beyond the Void had stirred.
Then the armor moved.
The knights’ faces turned pale.
CLICK.
The chest plate attached itself.
CLACK.
The gauntlets formed.
RATTLE.
The greaves locked into place.
The helmet descended.
Everything fit perfectly.
Like it had always belonged to me.
A one-handed black longsword materialized beside me.
Voidfang.
Azure cracks glowed across its blade.
The surrounding air distorted around the weapon.
The knights stared in disbelief.
One actually took a step backward.
"W-What monster are you?"
I smiled beneath the helmet.
"Round Two, fuckers"
BOOOOOOM!!!
The ground exploded.
I vanished.
CLANG!!!
The nearest knight raised his sword.
Too late.
SHATTER!!!
His weapon exploded into fragments.
His eyes widened.
PHUCH!
Voidfang pierced directly through his heart.
THUD.
His body collapsed.
The remaining four immediately attacked together.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
Sparks erupted everywhere.
Their swords struck my armor repeatedly.
But Velzareth remained untouched.
Not even a scratch.
Meanwhile—
SHATTER!
Another sword broke.
CRACK!
A punch caved in a knight’s breastplate.
Blood exploded from his mouth.
His internal organs shattered instantly.
The remaining three began panicking.
This wasn’t a battle anymore.
It was an execution.
"Retreat!"
One finally shouted.
The remaining knights immediately turned and ran.
PHUCH!
I threw Voidfang.
The sword became a streak of azure light.
One knight collapsed instantly.
The blade pierced directly through his back.
The final two desperately tried escaping.
"Impossible!"
"How is he this strong?!"
I activated Void Step.
WHOOOSH!
My body disappeared.
Then appeared directly behind one of them.
His entire body froze.
Cold sweat covered his face.
"How—"
BAM!
My fist smashed through his heart.
His chest exploded.
The last survivor immediately collapsed.
Fear had completely broken him.
"No!"
"Please!"
"I’ll become your slave!"
"I’ll tell you everything!"
He crawled backward desperately.
Blood covered his face.
His armor was completely ruined.
I slowly walked toward him.
As Voidfang teleport and appeared in my hands.
For a brief moment—
Hope appeared in his eyes.
Then I spoke.
"Interesting offer."
His face lit up.
"But I still prefer you dead."
"N-No wai—"
PHUCH!
Voidfang pierced his throat.
Silence returned.
The battlefield became still.
Five corpses.
Blood-stained grass.
Broken armor.
The setting sun.
I sighed.
"So much bloodshed."
I looked toward the distant mansion.
"Roland Ashenford."
I already knew who sent them.
No need to investigate.
After searching the bodies and collecting the silver coins, I dragged the corpses into nearby bushes.
Then I sat beneath a large tree.
The cool evening breeze brushed against my face.
Finally.
Some peace.
Then—
The System suddenly spoke.
[Reward calculated from emotional influence, Aurielle.]
[100x Return Activated.]
A grin slowly appeared on my face.
"Your timing really is perfect, System."
[Chapter End]

The moment the bags opened, the villagers crowded around in excitement.
Within minutes, all ten bags had been distributed.
"Good."
A satisfied smile appeared on my face.
I raised one of the remaining seeds and spoke loudly enough for everyone to hear.
"These aren’t ordinary wheat seeds."
The crowd immediately became attentive.
"I specifically brought these here."
"This wheat grows nearly ten times faster than normal crops."
"It also requires very little water and maintenance."
The moment those words left my mouth—
The entire crowd froze.
Their eyes widened.
Several farmers looked at the seeds in their hands as though they were holding treasure.
Because they understood exactly what this meant.
Normally, they would spend months waiting for a harvest.
Months of hard labor.
Months of uncertainty.
Months of praying that droughts, monsters, or bad weather wouldn’t destroy everything.
But now...
They could harvest far sooner.
Food shortages could finally ease.
For many families, this meant survival.
"Thank you, Sir!"
A middle-aged farmer suddenly shouted.
Soon others joined.
"Thank you!"
"Thank you, Young Master!"
"We’ll never forget this!"
I smiled and waved my hand.
Then I instructed Noah to organize the seed distribution and make sure everyone planted them today.
Noah nodded enthusiastically.
"I’ll take care of it, Young Master."
After everything was settled, I finally left the village alone and started walking back toward the mansion.
The sun had already begun setting.
Golden light stretched across the fields.
A cool breeze rustled the grass.
For a brief moment, everything felt peaceful.
Then—
Crunch.
A branch snapped.
I stopped walking.
My eyes narrowed.
Several armored figures stepped out from behind nearby trees.
Others casually emerged from the shadows.
Five men.
All wearing steel knight armor.
Their armor bore traces of long service.
Numerous scratches.
Dried blood stains.
Battle-worn capes.
Most importantly—
Every one of them radiated the aura of a Peak Iron Knight.
One of them smirked.
"Took you long enough, Young Master."
He paused before mocking laughter escaped his mouth.
"Or should I say..."
"Talentless Hero."
"Hahahahaha!"
The other four immediately burst into laughter.
I remained silent.
My eyes carefully observed each of them.
Professional soldiers.
Not bandits.
Not mercenaries.
These men had killed before.
A lot.
"Who sent you?"
I asked calmly.
The leader grinned and said something.
"You touched something that belongs to our lord."
His expression gradually became colder.
"The Baroness."
"Our lord has wanted her for years."
He slowly drew his sword.
CLING.
The blade reflected the evening sunlight.
"Now he wants your hands."
He pointed the sword toward me.
"And your manhood."
The others began surrounding me.
Like wolves cornering prey.
"Take your punishment."
BOOM!
Golden energy erupted from my body.
Titan Physique activated.
The ground beneath my feet cracked.
The five knights’ expressions changed slightly.
Then the leader charged.
BANG!
My fist slammed directly into his chest armor.
The steel immediately bent inward.
CRASH!
His body shot backward like a cannonball and smashed into the ground.
But before I could capitalize—
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
The remaining four attacked simultaneously.
Their coordination was excellent.
One targeted my head.
One my legs.
One my back.
One aimed directly for my heart.
CLANG!
I caught a sword with my bare hand.
Blood immediately appeared.
The blade cut through my skin despite the golden energy coating it.
"Damn."
BANG!
I punched the attacker across the jaw.
His helmet dented inward.
But another sword immediately slashed across my back.
SLASH!
Pain exploded through my body.
Blood sprayed.
A third knight stabbed toward my shoulder.
PHUCH!
The blade pierced flesh.
I gritted my teeth.
These weren’t weak opponents.
They were experienced Iron Knights attacking together.
BAM!
I kicked one away.
CRASH!
He smashed into a tree.
But moments later he stood again.
Injured.
Yet still fighting.
The first knight I had punched also staggered back to his feet.
Blood dripped from his mouth.
Yet his eyes remained vicious.
Five against one.
And they knew exactly how to work together.
"This is bad."
I dodged another thrust.
A sword barely missed my throat.
The tip sliced my cheek.
Blood trickled down.
Another attack came immediately after.
No openings.
No hesitation.
Only relentless pressure.
Then—
The System’s voice echoed.
[Luke.]
[You have reached Body Tempering Realm.]
[Second Form Available.]
[Summon the first armour.]
[Do it quickly.]
For the first time—
I heard urgency in the System’s voice.
I didn’t hesitate.
I raised my hand.
The surrounding world suddenly became silent.
"From the forgotten Void beyond time..."
The five knights paused.
The air itself felt wrong.
"Heed my command..."
Darkness spread.
Not physical darkness.
Something deeper.
Older.
A darkness that existed before light.
"Velzareth..."
Far above.
Beyond mortal sight.
Ancient beings sleeping in forgotten dimensions slowly opened their eyes.
Ancient gods paused.
Primordial entities looked toward the mortal world.
Something they had not seen for countless ages...
Had awakened.
"Warden of the Void Path."
The world froze.
For a fraction of a second—
Reality itself seemed to stop breathing.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
Void energy erupted.
The sky darkened.
Azure-blue runes illuminated the surroundings.
The five knights instantly fell to one knee.
Their faces filled with terror.
"What... what is this?!"
The leader shouted.
Then it appeared.
Inside an endless black void behind me—
A suit of ancient armor floated silently.
Velzareth.
Matte black armor.
Azure-blue runes flowing across its surface like living veins.
A dark cape swayed gently despite the complete absence of wind.
The armor radiated neither holiness nor malice.
Neither light nor darkness.
Only inevitability.
Like a silent executioner that had waited countless ages for its master to return.
CLINK.
CLINK.
CLINK.
The sound of chains echoed through the battlefield.
Then—
Twelve enormous Void Chains materialized around my body.
Each chain stretched endlessly into the surrounding Void, disappearing into unseen depths beyond reality itself.
Ancient.
Heavy.
Oppressive.
Like restraints forged to bind something that should never have existed.
The sight alone caused the surrounding Iron Knights to instinctively step back.
Among the twelve chains, only a single chain was connected to Velzareth.
The remaining eleven vanished into the endless darkness beyond the Void.
No one knew what lay at their other ends.
No one could see it.
Yet merely looking at those chains filled the heart with an indescribable sense of dread.
As if unimaginably terrifying beings slumbered beyond them.
As if Velzareth was only the first thing being restrained.
Then—
CRACK.
The chain connected to Velzareth shattered.
The sound echoed like a divine decree across heaven and earth.
For a brief moment, the remaining eleven chains rattled violently.
As though something beyond the Void had stirred.
Then the armor moved.
The knights’ faces turned pale.
CLICK.
The chest plate attached itself.
CLACK.
The gauntlets formed.
RATTLE.
The greaves locked into place.
The helmet descended.
Everything fit perfectly.
Like it had always belonged to me.
A one-handed black longsword materialized beside me.
Voidfang.
Azure cracks glowed across its blade.
The surrounding air distorted around the weapon.
The knights stared in disbelief.
One actually took a step backward.
"W-What monster are you?"
I smiled beneath the helmet.
"Round Two, fuckers"
BOOOOOOM!!!
The ground exploded.
I vanished.
CLANG!!!
The nearest knight raised his sword.
Too late.
SHATTER!!!
His weapon exploded into fragments.
His eyes widened.
PHUCH!
Voidfang pierced directly through his heart.
THUD.
His body collapsed.
The remaining four immediately attacked together.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
Sparks erupted everywhere.
Their swords struck my armor repeatedly.
But Velzareth remained untouched.
Not even a scratch.
Meanwhile—
SHATTER!
Another sword broke.
CRACK!
A punch caved in a knight’s breastplate.
Blood exploded from his mouth.
His internal organs shattered instantly.
The remaining three began panicking.
This wasn’t a battle anymore.
It was an execution.
"Retreat!"
One finally shouted.
The remaining knights immediately turned and ran.
PHUCH!
I threw Voidfang.
The sword became a streak of azure light.
One knight collapsed instantly.
The blade pierced directly through his back.
The final two desperately tried escaping.
"Impossible!"
"How is he this strong?!"
I activated Void Step.
WHOOOSH!
My body disappeared.
Then appeared directly behind one of them.
His entire body froze.
Cold sweat covered his face.
"How—"
BAM!
My fist smashed through his heart.
His chest exploded.
The last survivor immediately collapsed.
Fear had completely broken him.
"No!"
"Please!"
"I’ll become your slave!"
"I’ll tell you everything!"
He crawled backward desperately.
Blood covered his face.
His armor was completely ruined.
I slowly walked toward him.
As Voidfang teleport and appeared in my hands.
For a brief moment—
Hope appeared in his eyes.
Then I spoke.
"Interesting offer."
His face lit up.
"But I still prefer you dead."
"N-No wai—"
PHUCH!
Voidfang pierced his throat.
Silence returned.
The battlefield became still.
Five corpses.
Blood-stained grass.
Broken armor.
The setting sun.
I sighed.
"So much bloodshed."
I looked toward the distant mansion.
"Roland Ashenford."
I already knew who sent them.
No need to investigate.
After searching the bodies and collecting the silver coins, I dragged the corpses into nearby bushes.
Then I sat beneath a large tree.
The cool evening breeze brushed against my face.
Finally.
Some peace.
Then—
The System suddenly spoke.
[Reward calculated from emotional influence, Aurielle.]
[100x Return Activated.]
A grin slowly appeared on my face.
"Your timing really is perfect, System."
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Kneel or Die
paragraphs: After sitting down, I immediately asked,
"System, show me Velzareth’s description."
Then a translucent blue screen appeared before my eyes.
[Velzareth, Warden of the Void Path]
First Regalia of the Thirteen Eternal Armors
An ancient armor forged before recorded history.
Cloaked in darkness and marked by azure runes, Velzareth grants its wielder unmatched mobility and precision.
Current Ability:
Void Step
Allows instantaneous movement within 1 meter.
Current Compatibility:
Body Tempering Realm
I stared at the description with shining eyes.
If this was only the First Regalia, then there were still twelve more waiting to be unlocked.
A thrill ran through my body.
"I’ll unlock all of them one day."
I clenched my fist tightly.
The image of thirteen legendary armors standing behind me flashed through my mind.
DINGGG!
The sudden notification nearly made me jump.
[Reward calculated from emotional influence: Aurielle.]
[Emotional State: Happiness / Minor Trust]
[100x Return Activated.]
[As this is your first intercourse with wife Aurielle, an additional 100x Critical Multiplier has been applied.]
For a moment—
I froze.
Then my eyes widened.
My mouth slowly opened.
"...No way."
I rubbed my eyes.
Then checked again.
"...No freaking way."
A grin spread across my face.
"Finally!"
"A 10,000x Return!"
[Congratulations!]
Due to the 10,000x Return Effect, your reward has been upgraded from F-Rank to S-Rank.
[S-RANK FOUNDER’S PACKAGE]
Rewards Granted:
1. Blackstone Guardian Legion
• 1 Silver Knight Commander
• 10 Bronze Knights
• 100 Iron Knights
• 1,000 Body Tempering Soldiers
All troops are absolutely loyal and battle-tested veterans.
"System..."
I laughed.
"You really know me well."
Just this morning, I had been worried about Roland’s army.
Now I suddenly owned one.
Not just soldiers—
An actual army.
For the first time since arriving in this world, I finally felt a sense of security.
Then I moved to the next reward.
2. Mana Well
A permanent mana spring capable of continuously generating high-density mana.
Effects:
• Accelerates cultivation speed
• Improves magical crop growth
• Enhances mage training efficiency
• Gradually increases territory mana density
A smile appeared on my face.
"Perfect."
Blackstone Highlands desperately lacked resources.
With this alone, the territory’s future would completely change.
Warriors would grow stronger.
Mages would develop faster.
Even ordinary crops would improve.
3. Healing Spring
A natural healing lake infused with life energy.
Effects:
• Accelerates injury recovery
• Removes fatigue
• Increases soldier survival rate
• Slowly heals minor illnesses
"Good."
I nodded.
This wasn’t just useful.
It was life-saving.
A territory constantly fighting monsters and bandits needed healers.
But healers were expensive.
This spring could save hundreds of lives over the years.
4. Arcane Sky Tower
A mobile floating mage fortress.
Capabilities:
• Advanced camouflage
• Long-range spell bombardment
• Aerial reconnaissance
• Mobile command center
• Autonomous flight
Can silently travel across vast distances without detection.
My eyes nearly popped out.
"That’s cheating."
I’ve seen floating mage towers in fantasy novels and comics.
Every single one was terrifying.
They could transport elite forces.
Launch devastating magical bombardments.
Spy on enemies.
And serve as mobile fortresses.
Kingdoms would start wars for something like this.
5. Time Acceleration Chamber
A special dimensional training facility.
Time Ratio:
30 Days Inside = 1 Day Outside
Functions:
• Soldier Training
• Mage Training
• Cultivation
• Research and Development
• Skill Mastery
"Huh?"
I blinked.
Then blinked again.
"...Time?"
My heart skipped a beat.
No.
Forget S-Rank.
If someone called this an SSS-Rank treasure, I would believe them immediately.
Then a terrifying thought appeared in my mind.
I sat upright.
"Wait."
"What if I put the Mana Well and Healing Spring inside the chamber?"
The more I thought about it, the more ridiculous it became.
Soldiers could train for months.
Recover instantly.
Then continue training.
Mages could cultivate thirty times faster.
Researchers could spend years developing new techniques.
The entire territory could grow at an absurd speed.
"Amazing."
I couldn’t stop laughing.
For once—
The system had given me something truly insane.
Then another thought appeared.
I immediately shook my head.
"Actually..."
"I’ll use system rewards to become stronger."
"The soldiers can do the training."
I nodded seriously.
"Yeah."
"That’s words suite for a hero"
After leaving the reward screen, I began returning to the territory.
The afternoon sun slowly descended toward the mountains.
Cold winds swept across Blackstone Highlands.
Roughly thirty minutes later—
The lord’s estate finally came into view.
Then my footsteps stopped.
Smoke.
Fire.
Black smoke rose into the sky from inside the estate.
The distant glow of flames reflected against the surrounding buildings.
People had gathered outside.
Merchants.
Adventurers.
Travelers.
Local civilians.
Hundreds of them stood watching from a distance.
Not helping.
Simply watching.
Like spectators enjoying a performance.
My expression darkened immediately.
"Aurielle..."
"The mages..."
A bad feeling gripped my chest.
Then I heard nearby conversations.
"Looks like Blackstone Highlands is finally changing rulers."
A merchant sighed.
"Well, everyone knew this would happen."
"I saw Roland’s family army arrive last night."
Another man laughed mockingly.
"That exiled princess really thought she could hold this territory?"
"As long as her stepbrothers and stepsisters are alive, she never stood a chance."
Then his smile became disgusting.
"By now she’s probably Roland’s toy."
"That bastard is lucky."
"I heard she’s unbelievably beautiful."
"I’d pay anything for a single night—"
My eyes turned cold.
The world suddenly felt silent.
The man kept talking.
Completely unaware.
"And that useless Hero?"
Someone asked.
The same merchant snorted.
"A failure."
"Probably dead already."
"I bet Roland had him killed this morning."
Something inside me snapped.
BANG!!!
His head exploded.
Blood and bone fragments sprayed through the air.
The crowd froze.
For a heartbeat—
Nobody moved.
Then screams erupted.
"AAAAAHHH!"
"MURDER!"
"OH GODS!"
People stumbled backward.
Some fell to the ground.
Others ran.
Panic spread instantly.
I slowly lowered my blood-covered hand.
My expression remained calm.
Ice cold.
Then I spoke.
"The husband of Aurielle Valmont."
Silence.
"The Hero summoned by the Goddess."
More silence.
"Has arrived."
A chill spread through the crowd.
No one dared speak.
No one dared move.
STEP.
STEP.
STEP.
I walked forward.
People immediately moved aside.
An empty path formed before me.
Like subjects welcoming a king.
Ahead stood the estate gate.
Ten Iron Knights.
One hundred Body Tempering soldiers.
All armed.
All waiting.
The Iron Knights wore dark steel armor marked with Roland’s insignia.
Their faces were hard.
Scarred.
Experienced.
Yet I could see mockery in their eyes.
Because unlike the civilians—
They are not afraid of me.
I stopped before the gate.
The soldiers lowered their spears.
The Iron Knights unsheathed their swords.
Steel gleamed beneath the evening sunlight.
I looked at them calmly.
Then spoke.
"Answer my call."
A faint smile appeared.
"Velzareth."
BOOOOOOM!!!
Space shattered.
Dark-blue energy erupted from the void itself.
The surrounding air distorted violently.
Gasps erupted from the crowd.
Black armor emerged from darkness.
Ancient.
Majestic.
Terrifying.
Azure runes ignited across its surface.
CLICK.
CLACK.
CLICK.
One piece after another attached itself to my body.
The sound echoed like the march of death.
By the time the final piece locked into place—
Even the Iron Knights had gone pale.
The helmet vanished.
I rested Voidfang upon my shoulder.
The black blade reflected the burning mansion behind me.
The soldiers tightened their grips.
Sweat appeared on several foreheads.
I activated mana.
Then shouted.
"EVEN THOUGH YOU ARE MY SUBJECTS—"
BOOOOOOM!!!
My voice exploded across the territory.
Windows rattled.
Dust fell from rooftops.
Birds scattered into the sky.
People covered their ears.
Several civilians nearly collapsed from the pressure.
The soldiers flinched.
I pointed my sword toward them.
"FROM THIS MOMENT FORWARD—"
"ALL TRAITORS WILL BE EXECUTED!"
"HAVE NO EXPECTATION OF MERCY!"
The wind roared around me.
Smoke billowed through the air.
"THAT’S WHY SURRENDER NOW"
The blackstone gate guards exchanged nervous looks.
But then—
"HAAAH!"
One of Roland’s Iron Knights charged.
A tall man with a scar running across his face.
His sword flashed.
The other knights followed immediately.
Trying to overwhelm me before I could act.
I sighed.
"Sigh..."
Then snapped my fingers.
SNAP.
The world trembled.
Dozens.
Hundreds.
Thousands.
Massive magic circles appeared behind me.
They covered the entire road.
The earth shook violently.
The crowd screamed and ran.
The charging knights stopped dead in their tracks.
Their faces turned white.
WHOOOOOOOSH!!!
Armor clashed.
Boots struck the ground.
The Blackstone Guardian Legion appeared like a tide of steel.
One thousand soldiers.
One hundred Iron Knights.
Ten Bronze Knights.
And at the very front—
A Silver Knight Commander.
Her silver armor radiated overwhelming pressure.
The aura alone made Roland’s knights struggle to breathe.
The battlefield became silent.
The enemy soldiers stared in horror.
Their confidence shattered completely.
Their lips trembled.
Like they want to ask, does my offer still valid?
But I just smiled.
A cold smile.
Then raised Voidfang.
The gate guards looked at the legion.
Then at me.
Then at the Silver Knight Commander.
Their faces lost all color.
Fear filled their eyes.
And for the first time—
They realized they had chosen the wrong side.
[Chapter End]

"HAVE NO EXPECTATION OF MERCY!"
The wind roared around me.
Smoke billowed through the air.
"THAT’S WHY SURRENDER NOW"
The blackstone gate guards exchanged nervous looks.
But then—
"HAAAH!"
One of Roland’s Iron Knights charged.
A tall man with a scar running across his face.
His sword flashed.
The other knights followed immediately.
Trying to overwhelm me before I could act.
I sighed.
"Sigh..."
Then snapped my fingers.
SNAP.
The world trembled.
Dozens.
Hundreds.
Thousands.
Massive magic circles appeared behind me.
They covered the entire road.
The earth shook violently.
The crowd screamed and ran.
The charging knights stopped dead in their tracks.
Their faces turned white.
WHOOOOOOOSH!!!
Armor clashed.
Boots struck the ground.
The Blackstone Guardian Legion appeared like a tide of steel.
One thousand soldiers.
One hundred Iron Knights.
Ten Bronze Knights.
And at the very front—
A Silver Knight Commander.
Her silver armor radiated overwhelming pressure.
The aura alone made Roland’s knights struggle to breathe.
The battlefield became silent.
The enemy soldiers stared in horror.
Their confidence shattered completely.
Their lips trembled.
Like they want to ask, does my offer still valid?
But I just smiled.
A cold smile.
Then raised Voidfang.
The gate guards looked at the legion.
Then at me.
Then at the Silver Knight Commander.
Their faces lost all color.
Fear filled their eyes.
And for the first time—
They realized they had chosen the wrong side.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Betrayal Within the Walls
paragraphs: 1 Hour Earlier
Aurielle sat behind her officer’s desk, lost in thought.
A faint smile occasionally appeared on her face before disappearing again.
From the side, Margaret noticed the unusual expression and couldn’t help teasing her.
"Did something happen last night, My Lady?"
Aurielle nearly fell from her chair.
"W-What?!"
She quickly straightened herself and looked away.
"Ah... nothing happened."
Her voice lacked confidence.
Margaret simply smiled knowingly but chose not to push further.
BANG!!
The office door suddenly burst open.
Noah rushed inside, breathing heavily.
At first, Aurielle frowned at the interruption.
But seeing the panic on his face, her expression immediately changed.
"What happened?"
Noah bent forward while gasping for breath.
"My Lady... Lord Roland and several knights have revolted!"
"They’ve set fire to multiple barracks and tents!"
"Some loyal soldiers were still inside when the fires started!"
Aurielle’s face instantly darkened.
"What?"
Even though she never trusted Roland completely, she never expected such an open betrayal.
"My Lady, we have to do something."
Margaret’s voice carried obvious concern.
Aurielle immediately stood.
"Noah."
"Go call Sir Osric immediately."
As she spoke, Margaret had already opened a nearby cabinet.
Inside rested a black suit of armor accented with elegant purple patterns.
Noah froze.
His eyes widened.
He immediately recognized it.
The armor once belonged to Aurielle’s mother.
Then he nodded and sprinted away.
Aurielle quickly began putting on the armor with Margaret’s assistance.
As she fastened the final plate, she suddenly asked:
"Where is he?"
Margaret blinked, confused at first.
Then she understood.
"The Young Master?"
Aurielle nodded.
Margaret looked slightly embarrassed.
"My Lady... I don’t know."
Aurielle’s expression immediately tightened.
"But several guards and maids saw him leaving the territory this morning."
The moment she heard that answer, Aurielle became visibly worried.
Then she moved toward another cabinet.
CREEAK.
The door opened.
Inside rested a beautiful purple longsword decorated with intricate silver engravings.
Aurielle carefully picked it up.
"I told him Roland was dangerous."
She sheathed the sword at her waist.
"And now he’s wandering around outside."
Her voice carried both anger and concern.
Margaret could only sigh.
Soon both women left the office.
Outside, the smell of smoke already filled the air.
Black smoke rose from several locations within the estate.
Soldiers ran through the streets carrying water buckets while frightened servants hurried toward shelters.
The entire lord’s estate had descended into chaos.
After several minutes, they arrived at the military command room.
CREEAAAK.
The guards pushed open the heavy wooden doors.
Inside, a middle-aged knight stood beside a large strategic table.
A detailed map of Blackstone Highlands was spread across its surface.
His weathered bronze armor carried countless scratches and dents accumulated over years of warfare.
Dark-brown hair streaked with gray framed his scarred face.
The moment he noticed Aurielle’s arrival, he immediately straightened.
"Lady Aurielle."
He placed a fist against his chest.
Osric Thornfield.
One of Blackstone Highlands’ Bronze Knights.
A man who had defended this territory for more than twenty years.
Aurielle nodded.
"What is the situation?"
Osric’s expression darkened.
"My Lady..."
He pointed toward several marked locations on the map.
"Roland’s forces have completely surrounded the estate."
The atmosphere inside the room instantly became heavier.
Several Iron Knights clenched their fists.
"But if it’s only Roland and his followers, we can still suppress the rebellion."
Osric paused.
His jaw tightened.
Then he continued.
"The problem is... Roland brought his family’s army."
Silence.
The room froze.
Several knights stared at him in disbelief.
"What?"
Margaret’s face paled.
"No one reported their arrival?"
Aurielle asked.
Osric shook his head.
"They entered disguised as merchant escorts and knight retainers."
"They’ve been gathering inside the territory for days."
A chill spread through the room.
Only now did everyone realize how carefully Roland had prepared this betrayal.
One Iron Knight suddenly stepped forward.
"My Lady, we should retreat."
Another quickly nodded.
"He’s right."
"The territory cannot be saved anymore."
"We should escape and seek reinforcements from the border."
The moment the word border was mentioned—
Several expressions turned ugly.
Even Aurielle felt a headache coming.
There would be no help from the border.
Not now.
Not anytime soon.
"I refuse."
Aurielle’s voice echoed throughout the room.
Everyone turned toward her.
Her purple eyes burned with determination.
"We will suppress the rebellion."
"We will punish every traitor."
The room fell silent.
No one dared argue further.
Without another word, Aurielle turned and left.
Osric immediately followed.
Behind them, however, the remaining knights exchanged uneasy looks.
The moment the door closed—
One knight finally spoke.
"What should we do?"
His voice trembled slightly.
Another knight stood up.
"We leave."
Everyone looked toward him.
"I won’t betray Blackstone Highlands."
When they heard this, they sighed, thinking another fool.
But then—
He continued.
"But I also won’t throw my life away for a battle that’s already lost."
The room became silent again.
"Roland has already won."
One by one—
Several knights rose from their seats.
Some looked ashamed.
Others avoided eye contact entirely.
Yet none of them sat back down.
CREEAK.
The door opened.
Then closed.
Leaving only one Iron Knight behind.
A young man barely in his twenties.
His fists trembled with anger.
"Cowards..."
"They were born here."
"They grew up here."
"And now they’re abandoning it when it needs them most?"
His eyes burned with fury.
Without hesitation—
He rushed out after Aurielle.
Outside the command hall, Osric finally caught up with her.
"My Lady."
Aurielle stopped walking.
"I mean no disrespect..."
"But why?"
Osric looked directly into her eyes.
"Why stay?"
"The remaining knights will continue abandoning us."
Aurielle remained silent.
For several seconds, only the sound of distant flames could be heard.
Then she finally answered.
"Because of my husband."
Osric blinked.
He wasn’t expecting that answer.
Aurielle continued walking.
"I want to create a place where he can belong."
"A home."
Her voice softened slightly.
Then her expression hardened.
"And to do that..."
Her eyes narrowed.
"I must remove every piece of filth poisoning this territory."
A cold killing intent escaped her body.
Even Osric felt surprised.
Then—
CLAP.
CLAP.
CLAP.
Slow applause echoed from ahead.
Both immediately stopped.
Several figures emerged from the smoke-covered street.
At the front stood Roland.
Behind him were numerous armored knights.
Their swords were already drawn.
The atmosphere instantly became tense.
SHIIING!
Osric unsheathed his sword and stepped in front of Aurielle.
The blade pointed directly at Roland.
"Traitor."
Roland’s smile twitched.
Only slightly.
But it happened.
Then he sighed.
"Osric Thornfield."
"What a waste, you should have already joined me."
He slowly walked forward.
"You already know the state of this territory."
His gaze swept over the burning estate.
"Dying."
"Rotting."
"Abandoned."
He spread his arms.
"I’m simply doing what must be done."
Aurielle stared at him coldly.
Roland’s eyes landed on her.
"You should thank me."
"I’ll save Blackstone Highlands."
Then he smiled.
A smile filled with greed.
"And I’ll take care of its ruler as well."
Osric’s grip tightened.
BOOOOM!!
Bronze Knight aura exploded from his body.
The stone beneath his feet cracked.
A powerful shockwave blasted outward.
His cloak whipped violently behind him.
"That’s my answer."
Roland sighed.
"A shame."
He raised his hand.
Immediately—
Two Bronze Knights stepped forward.
BOOM!!
The ground shattered beneath their feet.
Both charged simultaneously.
CLANG!!!
Steel collided.
Sparks exploded into the air.
Osric was pushed backward several meters.
Stone tiles shattered beneath his boots.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
The three Bronze Knights exchanged blows so quickly that ordinary soldiers could barely follow their movements.
Shockwaves tore through nearby walls.
Windows exploded.
Wooden crates shattered apart.
A nearby soldier was thrown off his feet by the pressure alone.
Blood dripped from Osric’s shoulder after a sword grazed his armor.
Yet he continued fighting.
Like a veteran wolf cornered by hunters.
Meanwhile—
Roland moved along with two bronze knights.
BOOOOM!!
Bronze Knight aura erupted from his body.
The pressure crushed the surrounding ground.
Several weaker soldiers instinctively stepped back.
Aurielle immediately raised her sword.
Purple mana surged around her blade.
Despite being only a Peak Iron Knight—
Her aura was astonishingly stable.
Roland narrowed his eyes.
He knew why.
The blood of the empire still flowed within her veins.
That alone made her dangerous.
CLANG!!!
Their swords collided.
A powerful shockwave erupted.
The cobblestone street exploded beneath them.
Cracks spread in every direction.
Dust filled the air.
Aurielle slid backward several steps.
Roland remained standing.
Smiling.
Behind only one knight is standing and not joining the fight.
Aurielle noticed him immediately.
A dangerous feeling appeared in her heart.
But before she could think further—
Roland attacked again and other two bronze knights was aiming to subdue her.
BOOM!!
His blade descended.
Aurielle raised her sword.
KRAAAANG!!!
Sparks exploded.
A nearby stone pillar shattered from the impact.
Blood trickled from Aurielle’s palm where the vibration had torn her skin.
Roland smiled.
Then he leaned closer.
"Give up, Aurielle."
His voice carried absolute certainty.
"You’ve already lost."
[Chapter End]
