chapters.title: Chapter 18: Shadow Sovereign
paragraphs: After exchanging several blows with them, Aurielle realized she could no longer afford to hold back.
The three Bronze Knights were coordinating their attacks well, constantly forcing her to defend while Roland searched for an opening. If this continued, the battle would only drag on longer.
A cold look flashed through her eyes.
"Fine."
"You asked for this."
Aurielle slowly raised her hand.
The moment Roland saw her movement, a sense of danger surged through his heart. The other two Bronze Knights also became visibly wary.
"Dark Veil."
Her calm voice echoed across the battlefield.
The surrounding shadows immediately began stretching unnaturally.
WHOOOOOOOSH!
Dark mist burst outward like a black tide.
Shadows from shattered buildings, burning tents, and fallen soldiers seemed to come alive as darkness spread in every direction.
Within seconds, the battlefield was swallowed by an ocean of black.
Nearby soldiers immediately panicked.
"My vision!"
"I can’t see anything!"
"Stay together!"
Confused shouts echoed from all directions.
Even the sounds of battle became strangely muffled.
Roland’s expression changed.
"Quick! Use the Light Stone!"
His voice rang out, but even he noticed something was wrong.
The sound seemed weaker and Distant. As if the darkness itself was swallowing every noise.
Without wasting another second, Roland activated his C-Rank Origin Skill.
Infernal Core
*"A flame born within the heart. The longer it burns, the stronger its wielder becomes."*
THUMP.
A powerful heartbeat echoed from within his chest.
THUMP.
Crimson-orange light began glowing beneath his skin.
Deep inside his body, a burning core ignited.
From the outside, his chest faintly glowed through the gaps in his armor, while waves of heat spread from his body.
A Bronze Knight quickly activated a Light Stone.
A faint white glow pushed back part of the darkness, illuminating a small area around them.
Three shadows stretched beneath their feet.
The sight only made them more nervous.
"Where is she?"
One Bronze Knight asked while gripping his sword tightly.
Fear was already creeping into his voice.
His eyes continuously scanned the darkness.
A sudden scream shattered the silence.
"Behind you!!!"
The knight’s entire body froze. His pupils contracted.
Instinctively, he lowered his gaze. His own shadow... Was moving.
The darkness beneath his feet rippled like disturbed water.
A black-purple sword slowly emerged from it as Aurielle emerged alongside the blade.
CLANG!
The Bronze Knight reacted on pure instinct.
He raised his sword and blocked but the moment the two weapons collided—
BOOOOOOM!
A terrifying force erupted through his arms and his body was blasted backward.
CRASH!
He smashed through a broken wall before tumbling across the ground.
Dust and stone fragments exploded into the air.
Blood leaked from the corner of his mouth.
Roland’s eyes narrowed the moment he saw Aurielle emerge from the knight’s shadow, and he immediately activated:
Infernal Rush.
Fire gathered around Roland’s legs as the stone beneath his feet rapidly melted.
SSSSSSSS!
White steam billowed upward while intense heat distorted the surrounding air. Crimson flames wrapped around his lower body, and cracks spread across the ground beneath him.
BOOM!
A fiery explosion erupted beneath his feet.

Roland launched forward like a cannonball, tearing through the darkness at terrifying speed. A trail of flames was left behind in his wake, briefly illuminating the battlefield before being swallowed by the shadows once more.
To weaker soldiers watching from afar, it looked as though he had vanished entirely.
BANG!
Roland’s sword slammed into the ground with tremendous force.
Stone and dirt exploded upward as a shockwave rippled across the battlefield. Cracks spread through the earth, and a deep crater formed at the point of impact.
The attack was powerful enough to crush an Iron Knight instantly.
Yet—
The spot was empty as Aurielle had already disappeared.
Only faint ripples remained within the surrounding shadows, as if mocking Roland’s failed strike. His expression immediately darkened as he realized he had missed.
A ripple suddenly appeared behind the wounded Bronze Knight.
The shadows twisted and Aurielle stepped out once more.
Like a hunter emerging from the darkness.
Without wasting a single movement, she swung her Shadow Blade.
"What?!"
The Bronze Knight desperately raised his weapon.
SHATTER!
The moment the black-purple blade struck it, his sword exploded into fragments.
His eyes widened in horror as the Shadow Blade continued toward his neck without slowing.
The remaining Bronze Knight immediately rushed forward to rescue him.
Roland gritted his teeth and activated Infernal Rush once again.
Flames erupted beneath his feet.
His speed exploded.
Faster.
Faster.
Faster.
Yet no matter how desperately he moved—
He was still too late.
SLASH!
A black-purple flash crossed the darkness.
Silence.
For a brief moment, the Bronze Knight remained standing. Then a thin red line appeared across his neck.
PSHHH!

Blood erupted into the air. His expression froze as his head separated from his body and rolled across the shattered ground, leaving a crimson trail behind. The headless corpse swayed briefly before collapsing.
THUD!
The heavy sound echoed across the battlefield, causing several nearby soldiers to feel their hearts tremble. Even those outside the Dark Veil felt a chill run down their spines.
Aurielle’s figure dissolved back into the darkness once again, as if she had never been there.
"Damn it!"
Roland cursed while staring at the headless corpse, veins bulging across his forehead. Beside him, the remaining Bronze Knight’s expression completely changed as fear finally appeared in his eyes.
Inside this darkness, they weren’t hunting Aurielle.
Aurielle was hunting them.
Then he roared in anger.
"Do you think this darkness can stop me?!"
The flames around his body intensified.
Taking a deep breath, Roland drew upon the power of the Infernal Core and finally activated its true Origin Ability.
Infernal Awakening.
THUMP.
A powerful heartbeat echoed from within his chest.
THUMP.
The sound grew louder, heavier, and more violent with each beat as the temperature of the battlefield rapidly began to rise.
Then—
BOOOOOOM!
A wave of scorching heat erupted outward, forcing nearby soldiers to shield their faces as the burning air washed over them.

Crimson-orange cracks spread across Roland’s neck, arms, and face like molten lava flowing beneath his skin, while steam poured from his body in thick waves. His eyes ignited with a fiery orange glow, and the surrounding air visibly distorted from the intense heat.
Grass blackened and withered wherever the heat reached, while scattered wooden debris began to smoke and crackle.
Even the shadows covering the battlefield began to retreat beneath the overwhelming heat, shrinking back as if driven away by the blazing inferno radiating from Roland’s body.
The Dark Veil weakened significantly, and visibility gradually returned as the darkness slowly receded from the battlefield.
"There you are!"
Roland’s eyes immediately locked onto Aurielle’s silhouette.

She stood calmly amidst the fading darkness, her expression unchanged. The terrifying heat that was forcing soldiers to retreat and making the very air tremble seemed incapable of affecting her in the slightest.
Seeing her at last, Roland’s lips slowly curled into a confident grin.
Flames flickered wildly around his body as he activated another skill.
Blazing Cleave.
He burst forward, dragging his sword across the shattered ground as he charged.
SKRRRRAAAAAAPE!

A shower of sparks exploded behind him while Infernal Energy surged into the blade. The sword rapidly turned bright orange, its metal glowing as though it had just been pulled from a blacksmith’s furnace.
The surrounding temperature climbed even higher, forcing nearby soldiers to retreat instinctively. Some could already feel their skin burning despite the distance.
Roland roared and swung his sword.
SWOOOOOOOSH!
A gigantic crescent-shaped wave of fire erupted from the blade and tore across the battlefield like an unstoppable inferno.

The ground cracked apart beneath its path, stone melted into glowing slag, and everything it touched was reduced to ash. The sheer heat distorted the air, causing nearby soldiers to stumble backward in terror.
Yet Aurielle remained calm.
Her expression never changed as her eyes quietly followed the approaching attack.
Then she spoke.
"Time to end this."
Her voice was neither loud nor threatening.
Just calm.
Far too calm.
The moment Roland heard those words, a chill ran down his spine. His excitement vanished instantly, and his pupils contracted as an overwhelming sense of danger erupted within his heart.
Aurielle slowly raised her hand.
S-Rank Origin Skill.
Shadow Sovereign.
"The darkness obeys her call."
THUMP.
WHOOOOOOOSH!

Black mist flowed from Aurielle’s armor like smoke. Her purple eyes gradually darkened, and within them a faint violet glow slowly emerged. The ground around her became covered in moving shadows that slithered and twisted like living creatures responding to their ruler’s command.
Even the remaining Bronze Knight subconsciously took a step back. His instincts screamed at him.
Something terrifying was awakening.
Aurielle’s gaze never left the incoming wave of fire.
"Stop it."
A simple command.
Yet the shadows obeyed.

The surrounding darkness surged forward as countless shadows gathered together, twisting, compressing, and merging into one. Within moments, two gigantic shadow hands formed before her, each larger than a house. They stretched forward and seized the blazing sword arc head-on.
WHOOOOOSHHHHHH!
Fire and darkness collided.

Violent shockwaves erupted across the battlefield as the ground cracked beneath the pressure. The giant shadow hands trembled while the fiery crescent struggled violently, trying to force its way through. Flames exploded in every direction, scorching the earth and shattering nearby stone, yet the attack couldn’t advance even a single meter.
The strike that moments ago seemed capable of reducing everything in its path to ash was now completely restrained.
Roland’s eyes widened.
"Impossible..."
His voice trembled.

He knew exactly how powerful that attack was. With Infernal Awakening amplifying it, the strike had already touched the threshold of the Silver Knight Realm. Even most Bronze Knights would have been killed instantly.
Yet Aurielle had stopped it with a single command.
Before Roland could process what had happened, Aurielle’s mocking voice echoed from the darkness.
"An ant should know its place."
[Chapter End]

The three Bronze Knights were coordinating their attacks well, constantly forcing her to defend while Roland searched for an opening.
If this continued, the battle would only drag on longer.
A cold look flashed through her eyes.
"Fine."
"You asked for this."
Aurielle slowly raised her hand.
The moment Roland saw her movement, a sense of danger surged through his heart.
The other two Bronze Knights also became visibly wary.
"Dark Veil."
Her calm voice echoed across the battlefield.
The surrounding shadows immediately began stretching unnaturally.
WHOOOOOOOSH!
Dark mist burst outward like a black tide.
Shadows from shattered buildings, burning tents, and fallen soldiers seemed to come alive as darkness spread in every direction.
Within seconds, the battlefield was swallowed by an ocean of black.
Nearby soldiers immediately panicked.
"My vision!"
"I can’t see anything!"
"Stay together!"
Confused shouts echoed from all directions.
Even the sounds of battle became strangely muffled.
Roland’s expression changed.
"Quick!
Use the Light Stone!"
His voice rang out, but even he noticed something was wrong.
The sound seemed weaker and Distant.
As if the darkness itself was swallowing every noise.
Without wasting another second, Roland activated his C-Rank Origin Skill.
Infernal Core
*"A flame born within the heart.
The longer it burns, the stronger its wielder becomes."*
THUMP.
A powerful heartbeat echoed from within his chest.
THUMP.
Crimson-orange light began glowing beneath his skin.
Deep inside his body, a burning core ignited.
From the outside, his chest faintly glowed through the gaps in his armor, while waves of heat spread from his body.
A Bronze Knight quickly activated a Light Stone.
A faint white glow pushed back part of the darkness, illuminating a small area around them.
Three shadows stretched beneath their feet.
The sight only made them more nervous.
"Where is she?"
One Bronze Knight asked while gripping his sword tightly.
Fear was already creeping into his voice.
His eyes continuously scanned the darkness.
A sudden scream shattered the silence.
"Behind you!!!"
The knight’s entire body froze.
His pupils contracted.
Instinctively, he lowered his gaze.
His own shadow...
Was moving.
The darkness beneath his feet rippled like disturbed water.
A black-purple sword slowly emerged from it as Aurielle emerged alongside the blade.
CLANG!
The Bronze Knight reacted on pure instinct.
He raised his sword and blocked but the moment the two weapons collided—
BOOOOOOM!
A terrifying force erupted through his arms and his body was blasted backward.
CRASH!
He smashed through a broken wall before tumbling across the ground.
Dust and stone fragments exploded into the air.
Blood leaked from the corner of his mouth.
Roland’s eyes narrowed the moment he saw Aurielle emerge from the knight’s shadow, and he immediately activated:
Infernal Rush.
Fire gathered around Roland’s legs as the stone beneath his feet rapidly melted.
SSSSSSSS!
White steam billowed upward while intense heat distorted the surrounding air.
Crimson flames wrapped around his lower body, and cracks spread across the ground beneath him.
BOOM!
A fiery explosion erupted beneath his feet.
Roland launched forward like a cannonball, tearing through the darkness at terrifying speed.
A trail of flames was left behind in his wake, briefly illuminating the battlefield before being swallowed by the shadows once more.
To weaker soldiers watching from afar, it looked as though he had vanished entirely.
BANG!
Roland’s sword slammed into the ground with tremendous force.
Stone and dirt exploded upward as a shockwave rippled across the battlefield.
Cracks spread through the earth, and a deep crater formed at the point of impact.
The attack was powerful enough to crush an Iron Knight instantly.
Yet—
The spot was empty as Aurielle had already disappeared.
Only faint ripples remained within the surrounding shadows, as if mocking Roland’s failed strike.
His expression immediately darkened as he realized he had missed.
A ripple suddenly appeared behind the wounded Bronze Knight.
The shadows twisted and Aurielle stepped out once more.
Like a hunter emerging from the darkness.
Without wasting a single movement, she swung her Shadow Blade.
"What?!"
The Bronze Knight desperately raised his weapon.
SHATTER!
The moment the black-purple blade struck it, his sword exploded into fragments.
His eyes widened in horror as the Shadow Blade continued toward his neck without slowing.
The remaining Bronze Knight immediately rushed forward to rescue him.
Roland gritted his teeth and activated Infernal Rush once again.
Flames erupted beneath his feet.
His speed exploded.
Faster.
Faster.
Faster.
Yet no matter how desperately he moved—
He was still too late.
SLASH!
A black-purple flash crossed the darkness.
Silence.
For a brief moment, the Bronze Knight remained standing.
Then a thin red line appeared across his neck.
PSHHH!
Blood erupted into the air.
His expression froze as his head separated from his body and rolled across the shattered ground, leaving a crimson trail behind.
The headless corpse swayed briefly before collapsing.
THUD!
The heavy sound echoed across the battlefield, causing several nearby soldiers to feel their hearts tremble.
Even those outside the Dark Veil felt a chill run down their spines.
Aurielle’s figure dissolved back into the darkness once again, as if she had never been there.
"Damn it!"
Roland cursed while staring at the headless corpse, veins bulging across his forehead.
Beside him, the remaining Bronze Knight’s expression completely changed as fear finally appeared in his eyes.
Inside this darkness, they weren’t hunting Aurielle.
Aurielle was hunting them.
Then he roared in anger.
"Do you think this darkness can stop me?!"
The flames around his body intensified.
Taking a deep breath, Roland drew upon the power of the Infernal Core and finally activated its true Origin Ability.
Infernal Awakening.
THUMP.
A powerful heartbeat echoed from within his chest.
THUMP.
The sound grew louder, heavier, and more violent with each beat as the temperature of the battlefield rapidly began to rise.
Then—

Crimson-orange cracks spread across Roland’s neck, arms, and face like molten lava flowing beneath his skin, while steam poured from his body in thick waves.
His eyes ignited with a fiery orange glow, and the surrounding air visibly distorted from the intense heat.
Grass blackened and withered wherever the heat reached, while scattered wooden debris began to smoke and crackle.
Even the shadows covering the battlefield began to retreat beneath the overwhelming heat, shrinking back as if driven away by the blazing inferno radiating from Roland’s body.
The Dark Veil weakened significantly, and visibility gradually returned as the darkness slowly receded from the battlefield.

Roland’s eyes immediately locked onto Aurielle’s silhouette.
She stood calmly amidst the fading darkness, her expression unchanged.
The terrifying heat that was forcing soldiers to retreat and making the very air tremble seemed incapable of affecting her in the slightest.
Seeing her at last, Roland’s lips slowly curled into a confident grin.
Flames flickered wildly around his body as he activated another skill.
Blazing Cleave.
He burst forward, dragging his sword across the shattered ground as he charged.
SKRRRRAAAAAAPE!
A shower of sparks exploded behind him while Infernal Energy surged into the blade.
The sword rapidly turned bright orange, its metal glowing as though it had just been pulled from a blacksmith’s furnace.

Then she spoke.

Just calm.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: The Eternal Twilight
paragraphs: Before Roland could process what had happened, Aurielle’s mocking voice echoed from the darkness.
"An ant should know its place."
On this, he looked toward Aurielle and saw that she was preparing another spell.
His face instantly turned pale.
For the first time in many years, he felt something he had almost forgotten.
Death.
"Origin Ultimate Skill."
Aurielle’s voice echoed softly across the battlefield.
She slowly closed her eyes.
"Abyssal Execution."
The entire battlefield fell silent.
Every shadow within sight began moving toward her. Darkness flowed across shattered buildings, broken weapons, fallen corpses, and the blood-soaked earth before gathering behind her.
WHOOOOOOOOOM!
The mass of darkness continued growing larger and larger. It swallowed the surrounding light, twisted together, and compressed into a single point.
A gigantic black-purple blade slowly manifested behind Aurielle.
Dozens of meters long.
Towering above the battlefield like the weapon of a god.
The pressure alone caused the earth to crack.
Nearby soldiers dropped to one knee as fear gripped their hearts. Even the remaining Bronze Knights felt death looming over them.
Aurielle slowly opened her eyes.
Then she swung.
KRRRRRRAAAAAAAASHHHHHH!!!
A gigantic black-purple slash tore across the battlefield.
Buildings split apart as though they were made of paper. The earth cracked open beneath its path, while a devastating shockwave swept outward and sent countless soldiers flying.
Everything in its path was consumed.
The remaining Bronze Knights didn’t even understand what had happened.
One moment they were standing.
The next—
Their bodies split apart.
Blood erupted into the air as both halves crashed heavily onto the ruined battlefield.
Before the slash could continue any further, the cloaked knight who had remained silent the entire time finally moved.
A blur flashed across the battlefield.
The man instantly appeared in front of Roland and extended one hand forward.
When Roland saw him, hope finally appeared in his eyes.
"Uncle!"
Roland shouted.
BOOOOOOM!
The Abyssal Execution collided directly against the man’s outstretched hand.
The impact instantly shredded his dark cloak.
Pieces of cloth exploded apart, revealing thick brown hair and a rugged middle-aged face beneath.
WHOOOOSHHH!
"Ughhhh!"
The man gritted his teeth.
Veins bulged across his arm as he struggled to hold back the attack.
Even then, he was still being pushed backward.
The ground beneath his feet shattered.
Long trenches formed behind him as he desperately resisted the overwhelming force.
Yet a moment later, he roared.
"Don’t underestimate me!!!"
BOOOOOOM!
A terrifying aura erupted from his body.
Peak Silver Knight.
The pressure exploded across the battlefield.
WHOOOOSH!
Roland was blasted away instantly.
Nearby soldiers collapsed to the ground gasping for air while weaker men lost consciousness on the spot.
The surrounding ruins trembled violently.
Aurielle narrowed her eyes.
But she didn’t make another move.
Several moments later, the gigantic Abyssal Blade finally disappeared.
The battlefield slowly became visible again.
Everyone stared in shock.
The middle-aged man was still standing.
Blood dripped from the corner of his mouth.
One of his arms was completely ruined and covered in blood.
A massive trench stretched across the battlefield behind him.
Many soldiers could clearly see the dragging marks left behind as he had been pushed back nearly ten meters before finally stopping the attack.
The man spat blood onto the ground.
"Good kid."
He wiped his mouth and gave Aurielle a long look.
"Royal blood is still royal blood."
After saying that, he took out a healing potion and drank it.
Warm light spread across his body.
The ruined arm rapidly healed before everyone’s eyes.
A few seconds later, he casually swung it around.
"Good.
He then pulled out a sword.
Silver mana immediately surged across the blade.
The weapon released a sharp humming sound as he pointed it directly toward Aurielle.
"I’ll give you one last chance."
"Submit and accept Roland as your new husband."
A small smile appeared on his face.
Then he delivered the final blow.
"Because your useless Hero is dead anyway."
Silence.
Utter silence.
Even the battlefield seemed to freeze.
Many soldiers exchanged puzzled looks.
They didn’t understand why those words mattered.
But Aurielle did.
The color slowly disappeared from her eyes.
Her breathing quicken as her face pale and her pupils dialted.
Then Images start surfacing within her mind.
Luke.
His awkward smile.
His confused expression.
The way he looked at her without fear.
Without greed.
Without expectation.
Then the man’s words echoed again.
Dead.
Dead.
Dead.
The battlefield disappeared from her senses.
Only that single word remained.
When Aurielle finally spoke, her voice was so calm that it frightened everyone who heard it.
"Then why are you all still alive?"
Every person present instinctively looked toward her.
Their expressions froze.
Aurielle’s eyes had changed.
They were no longer purple.
They looked like glowing violet suns.
An overwhelming pressure began spreading outward.
Aurielle slowly spread her arms.
As her body descended toward the ground, light and darkness began flowing toward her from every direction.
Golden radiance and endless shadows intertwined around her figure, spiraling together like two rivers becoming one.
The moment her feet touched the ground, her body seemed to dissolve into the boundary between both forces.
Neither light.
Nor darkness.
But something that existed between them.
Then—
A sleepy, ancient voice echoed across the battlefield.
A voice so soft it was almost a whisper.
Yet every person present heard it clearly within their minds.
*"Lose yourself within the eternal dusk."*
The moment those words fell—
The sky dimmed.
Not darkened.
Dimmed.
The distinction between day and night slowly began to fade as if the world itself could no longer decide which side it belonged to.
Purple twilight mist emerged from every shadow.
From shattered walls.
From the cracked earth.
From pools of blood staining the battlefield.
From beneath the feet of every living being.
The mist spread endlessly.
Across the battlefield.
Across the horizon.
Across reality itself.
Tiny violet particles drifted through the air like fragments of dying stars, filling the world with an eerie and beautiful glow.
Then—
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH
The twilight mist erupted outward.
Yet strangely, no wind followed.
No sound accompanied its expansion.
The battlefield became unnaturally silent.
Even the clash of steel and the cries of soldiers seemed distant, as though swallowed by an invisible force.
The spreading mist moved like a dream invading reality.
The farther it expanded, the more distorted the world became.
Distances felt wrong.
Directions lost meaning.
Shadows stretched unnaturally.
And for a brief moment, every person caught within its embrace felt the same terrifying sensation—
"Twilight Veil".
When Darius Ashenford come out from trance, he looked around, and for the first time in many years, uncertainty appeared in his eyes.
The world had changed.
The battlefield was gone.
The burning tents, shattered walls, corpses, and blood-soaked earth had all vanished without a trace. In their place remained only an endless plain stretching toward the horizon.

Far in the distance, vast mountain ranges rose beneath a strange purple sky while enormous rivers wound through the land like silver serpents. Above them, the Sun and Moon existed together, hanging side by side in the heavens. Golden clouds drifted across violet skies, and countless stars glittered overhead despite it clearly being daytime.
The entire scene was breathtaking.
And horribly wrong.
Darius slowly tightened his grip on his sword.
This wasn’t an illusion.
His instincts were screaming at him.

It felt as though they had been dragged into another world, a place where the laws he understood no longer applied. A realm trapped between opposites. The moment before sunrise. The moment before sunset. A borderland suspended between beginnings and endings.
His gaze swept across the surroundings.
No soldiers.
No knights.
No sounds of battle.
Only one familiar figure remained.
Roland.
Darius immediately rushed toward him.
"Uncle! What is happening?"
Roland asked the moment Darius reached him. Panic was visible on his face, and even his voice sounded unstable.
Darius frowned.
"I don’t know."
Roland looked around once more, his eyes filled with growing unease.
"Is this related to the princess?"
Even he sounded uncertain asking the question.
Darius remained silent for several moments before finally speaking.
"We don’t know yet."
His eyes drifted toward the distant horizon.
"But it feels like we provoked something we should not."
A chill immediately ran down Roland’s spine.
After that, the two began searching.
Minutes passed.
Then hours.
They walked endlessly across the plain, yet nothing changed. No matter how far they traveled, the mountains never seemed any closer. The rivers remained distant. The horizon never moved.
It was as though the world itself refused to let them reach anything.
Eventually Roland’s frustration boiled over.
With an angry roar, he swung his sword.
BOOM!
A powerful shockwave erupted outward and tore across the landscape. The ground cracked apart as dust and stone exploded into the air.
Yet moments later—
The damage vanished.
The earth repaired itself before their eyes as though nothing had ever happened.
Roland froze.
Even Darius felt his heart sink.
Without saying a word, Darius raised his own sword.
Silver mana erupted from his blade.
WHOOOOSH!
A massive silver slash shot across the horizon and struck one of the distant mountains.
The entire peak split apart.
Rock collapsed.
Dust filled the sky.
For a brief moment, victory flashed across Roland’s face.
Then Darius blinked.
The mountain was whole again.
As though it had never been damaged.
Silence followed.
Neither man spoke.
For the first time since entering this strange world, genuine fear began creeping into their hearts.
An uncomfortable silence settled between them as they continued walking.
Eventually Roland stopped.
His breathing had become heavy.
His face was pale.
"Uncle..."
"What do we do now?"
Darius opened his mouth.
"Let me thi—"
His words stopped.
His entire body froze.
His pupils suddenly contracted.
Roland frowned.
"Uncle?"
Seeing Darius’s reaction, he quickly turned toward the direction his uncle was staring.
The moment he saw what stood in the distance—
The color drained from his face.
[Chapter End]

The entire peak split apart.
Rock collapsed.
Dust filled the sky.
For a brief moment, victory flashed across Roland’s face.
Then Darius blinked.
The mountain was whole again.
As though it had never been damaged.
Silence followed.
Neither man spoke.
For the first time since entering this strange world, genuine fear began creeping into their hearts.
An uncomfortable silence settled between them as they continued walking.
Eventually Roland stopped.
His breathing had become heavy.
His face was pale.
"Uncle..."
"What do we do now?"
Darius opened his mouth.
"Let me thi—"
His words stopped.
His entire body froze.
His pupils suddenly contracted.
Roland frowned.
"Uncle?"
Seeing Darius’s reaction, he quickly turned toward the direction his uncle was staring.
The moment he saw what stood in the distance—
The color drained from his face.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 20: After the Silence of War
paragraphs: The moment Darius and Roland saw what stood in the distance, both of them froze.

A massive moon hung above the horizon, so large it seemed to overshadow even the mountains. But its surface was fractured—cracks running through it like something had once tried to destroy it... and failed.
Then they saw the throne.
It was blurry, almost unreal, as if their eyes refused to fully accept it. And upon it sat a figure.
A woman with two violet suns where her eyes should have been.
The moment their gazes met hers, both of them felt something wrong—something beyond fear.
"W-what!!!"
"What’s happening—"
Their voices didn’t finish.
They broke apart mid-sentence, as if the sound itself had been cut away, and then their presence followed—erased completely, as though they had never been there at all.
Silence returned.
Finally, the being seated on the throne spoke.
"Aurielle... you should not have awakened me now."
She shook her head slowly, then lowered her gaze toward a golden chain that extended from her heart, its other end bound to a black-haired man.
"So you found someone..."
For a moment, it almost looked like she smiled.
Then even she began to fade, her form slowly being erased from existence.
"I hope you will survive this time..."
A faint, distant voice echoed—
Then—
SHATTER.
Reality broke apart.
And just as suddenly, everything returned to normal.
No throne remained.
No moon lingered in the sky.
No figure sat in the distance.
Only the battlefield was left behind—
And Blackstone’s soldiers, scattered across it, slowly beginning to rise in confusion.
"What... happened?"
"I don’t know... I think I just blacked out..."
They looked around in confusion, slowly realizing something was wrong.
The enemies were gone. All of them.
"Aurielle!"
A sudden voice cut through the confusion.
They turned toward it and saw a young man with black hair, wearing black-blue armored knight gear, running toward the center of the battlefield.
In an instant, awareness returned to the soldiers. One after another, they began moving as well, rushing toward the same direction.
"My lord, are you alright?"
Osric reached her first, stopping beside Aurielle and looking down at her anxiously.
But she didn’t respond.
She was unconscious.
Soon, Luke arrived with the silver knight at his side. His gaze immediately fell on Aurielle—no wounds, no visible injuries, yet completely unresponsive.
"Move aside."
Luke’s voice was firm.
Osric hesitated for a moment, exchanging a glance with him, then reluctantly stepped back.
Luke carefully lifted Aurielle into his arms.
Without another word, he turned and began walking toward the mansion.
But as he walked, his voice carried an order behind him.
"Kill the traitors. If they surrender, subdue them."
"Yes, sir!"
A loud response echoed across the battlefield.
As more than a thousand voices from the Blackstone Guardian Legion followed.
The unified roar shook the surroundings, startling even the nearby soldiers who had just regained consciousness.
As I reached the mansion gate and pushed it open, Margaret’s rushing figure appeared in front of me.
She was breathing heavily, panic clear in her voice as she asked,
"What happened to my lady?"
I shook my head.
"I don’t know... but let’s take her to Elena. Maybe she can help."
Margaret nodded quickly, worry still written across her face.
Soon, we reached Elena’s room. Since the mages had been assigned separate quarters, she was likely inside.
KNOCK-KNOCK
"Elena, are you inside?" I called.
A moment later, the door opened. Elena stood there in a nightgown, still half-awake. Without wasting time, I gently placed Aurielle into her arms and immediately turned away.
"Elena, please check her condition," I said without looking back.
She froze for a moment, clearly confused, then glanced down at herself. Her face turned slightly red as she spoke in a soft, shy voice.
"Yes... master."
The door closed.
I waited outside for a few moments.
Then Elena’s voice came from inside.
"Master... she seems fine. Just exhausted."
I turned back and looked inside. Margaret was carefully taking care of Aurielle, while Elena—now properly covered with a coat—looked at me for instruction.
"Good. Take care of her. If you need anything, tell me."
I said it calmly, then turned away and walked out again.
There was still a rebellion to deal with.
Someone had to restore order.
The moment I stepped outside, the sounds of chaos reached me again.
Pleas, begging, and desperation spread across the broken battlefield, turning orderless voices into a single wave of panic.
"Don’t kill me! I was brainwashed by Roland!"
"Please! We didn’t know the truth!"
I ignored the chaos behind me and approached Osric. The guilty ones would be sent to the mines later.
He was still directing the soldiers when I reached him.
"Osric, how is the situation?" I asked.
He turned toward me and let out a deep, tired sigh.
"Situation is very bad, young master.
He paused for a moment, gathering his thoughts before continuing.
"We’ve lost nearly seventy percent of our forces. Only a few remain now—most of them wounded... some even crippled."
His face looked older as he spoke, as if each word carried weight on his shoulders.
I nodded grimly. I could already see the truth of it around us.
Then I spoke, trying to steady the broken morale.
"Don’t worry. My soldiers will handle the burden and make up for the losses."
At my words, his expression eased slightly.
Behind him, hundreds of Iron Knights stood in formation, along with dozens of Bronze Knights. The sight alone seemed to restore a bit of hope in him.
"Thank you, young master. If the lord were here, she would be very happy," Osric said with a faint smile.
I nodded again.
Then I asked about the damages.
His expression darkened immediately.
"Young master... Roland burned nearly half of the military facilities. Many buildings were destroyed during the battle, and even more collapsed afterward."
I looked around.
Broken walls. Burned structures. Shattered stone scattered across the ground. And among them—silent corpses covered in dust.
A territory that had barely survived a disaster.
"Give them proper burial rites. Honor those who died protecting this land," I said quietly.
Then I took out a pouch of gold and placed it in his hands.
"Use this to compensate their families. Repair the structures. Rebuild what was lost."
Osric stared at the pouch for a moment. The weight of it was enough to shift the mood in his eyes.
With this, the territory might actually survive the aftermath.
"God has blessed our territory... to have you, young master," he said, voice trembling slightly with gratitude.
I simply nodded.
After that, I dismissed him and called the silver knight over.
I led the silver knight to Aurielle’s room.
Standing at the entrance, I gave my order in a low voice.
"Guard this place. Only allow entry with Margaret’s permission."
She nodded immediately without a hint of hesitation.
Her posture straightened as she took position outside the door, as if the entire corridor now belonged under her watch.
I then relayed the same order to Margaret.
She froze for a moment, clearly shocked. A Silver Knight was not an ordinary existence—such figures were rarely seen outside Viscount-level or higher territories.
In the Blackstone Highlands, there was only one Silver Knight, a relic brought by the Lord’s mother long ago, now stationed at the border as its silent guardian.
"...Thank you," Margaret said softly, her voice calmer now, though still carrying disbelief.
I gave a small nod in return.
My gaze lingered for a moment on Aurielle’s resting figure inside the room.
After a brief silence, I turned away.
It was time to rest.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Don’t Leave Me Again
paragraphs: Morning
As I woke up, I felt refreshed from the previous fights. I washed up and headed straight toward Aurielle’s room to check her condition.
"Good morning, young master."
As I passed through the hallways, many maids and guards greeted me with respectful bows.
"Seems like they already know about yesterday," I muttered under my breath, a faint smile appearing on my face.
The estate felt quieter than usual, yet there was a strange tension in the air, maybe they are worried what will happen next.
As I reached her room, I saw Aurora Valcrest still standing guard outside the door, sword in one hand and shield in the other.
Her long silver-white hair fell neatly over her armor, and her eyes glowed with a calm silver-blue light.
She wore black-silver knight armor engraved with thin glowing runes that pulsed softly with covenant energy, giving her an almost sacred presence under the dim corridor light.
"Master."
The moment I approached, she knelt in front of me without hesitation.
I smiled slightly. "Good. I’m satisfied with your performance."
"It is my duty, master. Anything for you."
She replied in a reverent tone, but something about it felt... overwhelming. Her devotion carried a strange intensity, almost unnatural, as if even loyalty itself had taken physical form around her.
"Cough..."
I lightly coughed to break the awkward atmosphere, then stepped inside.
Inside the room, Margaret was asleep on a chair, her head tilted slightly forward from exhaustion. Aurielle, however, still had not awakened.
I walked closer to her bed.
"Margaret, go and rest properly. I’ll take care of Aurielle," I said softly.
Margaret startled awake immediately, clearly caught off guard, but when she saw me, her expression eased.
"Don’t startle me like that, young master," she said with a tired but relieved tone.
I simply smiled.
She gave Aurielle one last worried glance before quietly leaving the room.
I sat beside Aurielle’s bed, my gaze lingering on her peaceful face.
"When will you wake up, darling..." I muttered softly.
Then I picked up a book Osric had given me and began reading. It contained information about Blackstone Highlands and its basic problems.
"So this territory has large reserves of blackstone... used to forge knight armor."
I raised my eyebrows slightly in surprise. No wonder Cedric’s noble were always trying to seize this land.
"The territory also doesn’t have a stable water source. Food is heavily dependent on farming, and there isn’t enough income to import supplies."
"Many bandits operate around the highlands, blocking merchants and weakening trade..."
I closed the book slowly.
"I’ll fix it one by one."
With that, I placed the book aside and closed my eyes for a short nap.
After a while—
"LUKE!!!"
A sharp, panicked voice suddenly pulled me awake.
I turned immediately toward Aurielle.
She was still asleep, but her expression was tense, her body slightly trembling as she muttered my name in her sleep.
"She’s having a nightmare..."
I quickly placed my hand on her cheek and spoke softly.
"I’m here, Aurielle. Don’t worry."
The moment my words left my mouth—
Her eyes suddenly snapped open.
And the moment she saw me in front of her, she immediately pulled me into a tight hug.
"Luke... thank god you’re safe..."
Her voice trembled with relief and panic mixed together. Before I could respond, she started kissing my face repeatedly, as if afraid I would disappear the next second.
"Don’t leave me again... promise me..."
"I won’t leave. I’m here, Aurielle," I said softly, patting her back.
Gradually, her shaking slowed. She leaned against my chest, breathing uneven but calming down.
Then she looked directly into my eyes.
I smiled and gently kissed her lips.
For a moment, everything else disappeared.
After a minute, we slowly separated.
"Huff... huff..."
We both caught our breath, but she was far calmer now. She rested her head against my chest again, holding onto me tightly.
"What happened earlier?" she asked quietly.
Then she added, her voice turning slightly distant,
"I don’t remember anything after my fight with Roland..."
"I reached there... but Roland’s army was gone. It was like they had been disappeard," I said, watching her reaction closely.
Her brows furrowed in confusion.
Then panic slowly returned to her eyes.
"Luke... this is bad. Very bad."
She grabbed my clothes tightly.
"What is it?" I asked calmly, holding her steady. "I’m here. Just tell me."
She took a deep breath, trying to control herself.
"Roland Ashenford is a noble... and also the youngest son of Viscount Ashenford."
She met my gaze again, her expression heavy.
"And that silver knight who stopped my attack... also seems to be from the Ashenford family."
My expression slowly changed.
"So now two nobles, along with their armies... have disappeared inside our territory," she said, her voice trembling.
"And?"
I urged her gently.
She hesitated, gripping my hands tighter.
"As you know... we can’t kill nobles. They will claim we did. Even if they just disappeared."
"The Viscount can now openly launch a campaign against us... and wipe out our entire territory if he wants."
Silence fell between us for a moment.
The weight of it settled heavily in the room.
I gently held her trembling hands.
"Aurielle... no one can do anything to you or this territory as long as I’m alive."
I leaned forward and kissed her forehead gently.
"So don’t worry. If they come... they will regret it."
Her shaking slowly stopped. Her expression softened, though worry still lingered in her eyes.
Then I told her about my tour regarding the territory
She immediately began giving me a lecture in a frustrated tone.
"I already dealt with the water and food problems inside the territory," I said, showing her the Aqua Crystals and explaining the mana wheat seeds.
"Wow... I’ve seen these things before, but I was never able to afford them," she muttered in surprise.
Then she looked at me with warm, affectionate eyes.
"My husband is really a capable man... huhu."
My face turned slightly red as I scratched the back of my head.
Then I teased her back.
"Well, you already knew that... since you were the one begging me to stop in bed."
Her entire face turned bright red instantly.
Even her ears flushed as she remembered their first night.
"Shameless..." she muttered under her breath.
I ignored her reaction and continued.
"Also, I summoned a new subordinate."

"Aurora Valcrest, come inside." I called her in, but if someone was here and saw them, then they can see Aurielle face become cold and her eyes narrowed as she dangerously looked toward the Luke and door. and was muttering something in very low voice like she wants to kill someone.
"Another woman..."
"...another woman..."
CREEK
The door opened and Aurora come inside, but then I heard Aurielle cold voice, "Husband don’t tell me that she is also send by your goddess of luck?"
Her voice seems different but while turning I replied as usual, "yes"
That single word was enough.
Aurielle suddenly grabbed my neck and started shaking me violently.
"Am I your enemy?! Is that why she keeps sending women after my husband?!"
"Does she not want me to be happy?!"
"Stop—Aurielle—wait—!"
I hurriedly waved my one hand toward Aurora who was about to attack Aurielle, then trying to calm her down, but nothings is working , as her eyes become deep purple and she has lost it.
Auroro looked worriedly toward her master and the crazy women, who seems to his wife.
When Aurielle was not calming down, I finally used the move, that I have watched in my previous world, that every husband do.
SMOOCH.
I grabbed Aurielle firmly and kissed her while hugged her tight.
The entire room went silent.
Her resistance weakened instantly.
Her grip loosened.
And slowly... she stopped shaking me.
"Mhmm..."
Her body relaxed as she melted into the kiss.
After a few minutes, I gently pulled back.
"Huff... huff..."
She gasped for air, slowly returning to normal. Her eyes regained their usual purple tone.
"Are you okay?" I asked softly.
"...yeah..." she muttered, slightly dazed.
But the moment she saw Aurora again—
She immediately clung to me like a cat guarding its territory.
I sighed.
"Aurielle... don’t behave like this. She guarded you all night. She’s also my loyal subordinate."
Aurora immediately knelt again.
But—
"Ouch!"
Aurielle suddenly bit my hand in frustration.
"So you’re taking her side now too..."
Her tone turned dangerously emotional again.
I exhaled slowly.
This was going to take a while.
After calming her down for a few more minutes, I finally explained Aurora’s Origin Skill.
"She has an A-Rank Origin Skill called Argent Covenant Authority."
I paused slightly, even I still found it unusual.
Her ability description was simple.
I repeated it slowly.
*"A vow is not spoken for meaning. It is spoken for consequence."*
[Chapter End]

"Well, you already knew that... since you were the one begging me to stop in bed."
Her entire face turned bright red instantly.
Even her ears flushed as she remembered their first night.
"Shameless..." she muttered under her breath.
I ignored her reaction and continued.
"Also, I summoned a new subordinate."

"Aurora Valcrest, come inside." I called her in, but if someone was here and saw them, then they can see Aurielle face become cold and her eyes narrowed as she dangerously looked toward the Luke and door. and was muttering something in very low voice like she wants to kill someone.
"Another woman..."
"...another woman..."
CREEK
The door opened and Aurora come inside, but then I heard Aurielle cold voice, "Husband don’t tell me that she is also send by your goddess of luck?"
Her voice seems different but while turning I replied as usual, "yes"
That single word was enough.
Aurielle suddenly grabbed my neck and started shaking me violently.
"Am I your enemy?!
Is that why she keeps sending women after my husband?!"
"Does she not want me to be happy?!"
"Stop—Aurielle—wait—!"
I hurriedly waved my one hand toward Aurora who was about to attack Aurielle, then trying to calm her down, but nothings is working , as her eyes become deep purple and she has lost it.
Auroro looked worriedly toward her master and the crazy women, who seems to his wife.
When Aurielle was not calming down, I finally used the move, that I have watched in my previous world, that every husband do.
SMOOCH.
I grabbed Aurielle firmly and kissed her while hugged her tight.
The entire room went silent.
Her resistance weakened instantly.
Her grip loosened.
And slowly... she stopped shaking me.
"Mhmm..."
Her body relaxed as she melted into the kiss.
After a few minutes, I gently pulled back.
"Huff... huff..."
She gasped for air, slowly returning to normal.
Her eyes regained their usual purple tone.
"Are you okay?" I asked softly.
"...yeah..." she muttered, slightly dazed.
But the moment she saw Aurora again—
She immediately clung to me like a cat guarding its territory.
I sighed.
"Aurielle... don’t behave like this.
She guarded you all night.
She’s also my loyal subordinate."
Aurora immediately knelt again.
But—
"Ouch!"
Aurielle suddenly bit my hand in frustration.
"So you’re taking her side now too..."
Her tone turned dangerously emotional again.
I exhaled slowly.
This was going to take a while.
After calming her down for a few more minutes, I finally explained Aurora’s Origin Skill.
"She has an A-Rank Origin Skill called Argent Covenant Authority."
I paused slightly, even I still found it unusual.
Her ability description was simple.
I repeated it slowly.
*"A vow is not spoken for meaning.
It is spoken for consequence."*
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 22: A Spring, A Well, and A Jealous Wife
paragraphs: "System, show me her first ability," I said.
Then a blue translucent window immediately appeared before me.
Ability 1
Argent Binding Chains
Silver chains manifested from covenant energy.
Effects:
• Binds multiple enemies at once
• Chains strengthen when resistance or betrayal intent is shown
• Restricts movement and weapon use
• Becomes stronger against those who have spoken or accepted terms
"Good," I muttered.
I then explained the ability to Aurielle as well.
"Well, she can form chains of oaths and bind anyone with them."
"So if someone betrays us or harbors hostile intent, she will know instantly and suppress that person immediately."
Aurielle’s expression changed when she heard that. Suddenly, Aurora seemed much more pleasing to her eyes.
However, her mouth fell completely open when I told her about the Time Chamber, Mana Well, and Healing Spring.
"Luke, this is absurd. No one can give away so many things."
Aurielle looked at me suspiciously.
At that moment, the system’s mocking voice rang out.
[Go ahead. Use her name more. I’m telling you, the day the Goddess of Luck finds out you’re using her name as an excuse, she’ll come looking for you herself.]
I ignored the system’s ridicule and Aurielle suspicous gaze.
Then I stood up.
"So, Aurielle, is there any place where we can put these?" I asked.
She thought for a moment.
"Ah... yes. Let’s go there."
With that, she led us deeper into the mansion.
All the guards and maids greeted us respectfully as we passed by.
After walking for nearly five minutes, we finally reached the basement alongside Aurora.
"Here."
Aurielle stopped.
I looked around and realized it was some sort of treasury.
Ten Iron Knights stood guard around the area, while numerous magic circles glowed faintly across the walls and floor.
THUD.
The moment they saw Aurielle, all ten knights knelt at once.
"Lord!"
"At ease," Aurielle ordered calmly.
The knights immediately stood back up and returned to their positions.
CREEEEAK...
The guards pushed open a massive metal door.
The heavy gate slowly swung inward with a deep metallic groan.
The three of us entered together, though I noticed several guards giving both me and Aurora curious looks.
Inside, stacks of armor, gold coins, silver coins, and various expensive treasures were neatly stored.
Aurielle then guided us toward a special hidden room.
"Here."
I followed her gaze and finally noticed a nearly invisible door hidden within the silver-colored wall.
"Okay."
Stepping forward, I gave the command.
"System, use the Time Chamber."
WHOOOOOOSH—
An intense surge of energy erupted from the hidden door.
Dark ripples spread across its surface like black ink swallowing silver metal.
The entire door gradually transformed into a pitch-black gate.
Then—
BZZZZT...
An Infinity Symbol slowly appeared upon its surface.
Countless tiny words formed its shape, endlessly shifting and moving.
I couldn’t understand a single one of them.
Yet merely looking at them made my head feel slightly dizzy.
BOOM.
Without warning, the gate swung open by itself.
Beyond it was a long black tunnel stretching into the unknown.
"Let’s go."
I looked toward Aurielle and Aurora.
Aurielle immediately grabbed my hand.
Aurora quietly hugs my hands, as I can feel her melons.
The next second, I felt a murderous gaze coming from my right side.
I wisely chose to ignore it.
Then the three of us stepped into the tunnel.
WHOOOOOSH...
The world around us blurred.
For a few moments, only darkness remained.
Then a brilliant light suddenly flooded our vision.
Instinctively, all of us closed our eyes.
When I finally opened mine again—
I froze.
A small world stretched before us.
A shining sun hung high in the sky.
Mountains rose in the distance.
Rivers flowed across vast plains.
Green grass swayed beneath the wind.
Forests stretched toward the horizon.
And standing quietly at the center of it all was a small wooden hut.
I heard both Aurora and Aurielle gasp in amazement.
Honestly, I felt the same.
"I can already feel that the mana here is denser than outside."
Aurielle slowly walked forward while touching the grass beneath her feet.
"It’s even higher than the cultivation chambers in the royal palace."
Her voice was filled with disbelief.
After discussing it for a while, we eventually found a suitable location in the distance for the new structures.
As I attempted to place the Mana Well and Healing Spring—
A massive 3D blueprint suddenly appeared before me.
Countless glowing lines spread across the ground.
I adjusted the positions carefully and finalized their locations.
The moment I confirmed—
RUMBLEEEEE—
The entire Time Chamber trembled violently.
The ground beneath our feet shook.
Aurielle instantly grabbed onto my arm.
Then—
BOOOOOOOM!
The earth split apart.
Massive chunks of soil and stone rose from below.
The structures emerged from the ground as if they had existed there for centuries.
The Mana Well rose first.
Then the Healing Spring followed.
The sight was both majestic and overwhelming.
"That was scary..."
Aurielle muttered while tightly clinging to me.
I looked down at her and couldn’t help but smile.
"How cute."
Then I looked toward the structure.
The Mana Well stood at the center of a circular stone platform carved from pale silver-blue stone.
Ancient runes glowed faintly along the edge of the platform, pulsing rhythmically like a heartbeat.
The well itself was constructed from smooth white stone that seemed untouched by time.
Instead of ordinary water, a swirling pool of liquid mana rested within it.
The liquid shimmered in shades of blue, violet, and silver, constantly rotating in slow circles.
Tiny particles of light drifted upward from the well like fireflies, disappearing several meters above the surface.
A cool breeze carrying rich mana spread continuously from the structure.
Even standing nearby made my mind feel clearer and my body lighter.
Around the well, patches of grass appeared noticeably greener than the surrounding land.
Small flowers bloomed naturally between the stones, nourished by the dense mana radiating from its core.
The deeper I looked into the well, the harder it became to tell whether I were staring at liquid mana... or an endless star-filled sky hidden beneath the surface.
"Cool!"
Soon, both Aurora and Aurielle rushed toward the Mana Well.
They immediately crouched beside it and dipped their hands into the glowing liquid mana to test it.
Aurielle even scooped up a handful and tasted it.
The moment it touched her tongue, her eyes lit up.
"Luke, come taste it! I’ve never tasted such pure liquid mana before!"
She waved excitedly at me.
I smiled and walked over to them.
As I reached the well, I lowered my hand into the shimmering liquid.
"It’s cold..."
The moment my fingers touched it, I felt a pleasant chill spread across my skin.
The liquid mana flowed between my fingers like water, yet felt far lighter and smoother.
Curious, I brought a small amount to my mouth and tasted it.
The moment it touched my tongue, I froze.
"...Sweet."
That was the only word that left my mouth.
It tasted like honey, yet not quite honey.
The sweetness was light and refreshing, carrying a faint coolness that spread through my body the moment I swallowed it.
Even the mana inside my body seemed to become slightly more active.
For a brief moment, I understood why Aurielle had looked so excited.
Then I looked toward the Healing Spring.
The Healing Spring emerged from the earth like a natural sanctuary blessed by life itself.
At its center stood a beautiful white stone fountain engraved with delicate leaf-shaped patterns and ancient life runes.
A continuous stream of crystal-clear water flowed from the top of the fountain, cascading down into the spring below.
The water carried a gentle emerald and golden glow, releasing countless specks of green light as it flowed.
Unlike ordinary water, it seemed alive.
Soft ripples spread across the surface of the spring even without wind, as if responding to the life energy constantly pouring into it.
The pool surrounding the fountain was several meters wide and perfectly clear, allowing the bottom to be seen despite its depth.
The spring was surrounded by smooth white stones polished by nature, forming a beautiful natural basin.
Vines covered with small silver flowers wrapped around the edges, while vibrant grass and blooming plants spread outward in every direction.
The air around the spring felt noticeably different.
Warm and comforting.
Simply standing nearby made exhaustion fade from my body.
A faint fragrance resembling fresh rain, wildflowers, and forest leaves continuously spread from the water.
What surprised me most was that despite the fountain endlessly pouring healing water into the spring, the water level never changed.
It neither overflowed nor decreased.
It was as if the spring maintained a perfect balance by itself.
I moved toward the Healing Spring and removed all my clothes.
"Kyahhh!!!"
Aurielle screamed and hastily covered Aurora’s eyes before she could witness her master’s majesty.
Aurielle immediately narrowed her eyes and leaned closer to Aurora’s ear.
"Did you just tch?" she asked in a cold voice.
Aurora was startled by the sudden voice beside her ear.
"No, miss. Why would I do that?" she replied innocently.
But Aurielle remained suspicious.
*"Did that goddess really send her to steal my husband?"* she thought.
Before she could question her further, Luke’s voice rang out from the spring.
"Both of you come here and take a bath as well! It feels amazing!"
Aurielle turned toward Luke.
He was already submerged in the spring and waving excitedly at them.
Reluctantly, she removed her hands from Aurora’s eyes.
As the two of them walked toward the spring, Aurora suddenly heard Aurielle’s threatening voice.
"Don’t you dare go fully nude."
Aurora paused slightly.
Aurielle walked past her while giving her a deadly glare.
Then, without hesitation, she removed her own clothes and jumped into the spring.
SPLASH.
"Gulp."
Aurora swallowed nervously.
After a moment, she removed everything except her innerwear and jumped in as well.
SPLASH.
"Wow, this feels great!"
Both Aurielle and Aurora exclaimed after submerging themselves in the spring.
The healing water immediately began reducing their fatigue while slowly healing hidden injuries throughout their bodies.
"Right?" I said with a grin.
A moment later, I heard Aurielle’s excited voice.
"Husband! We can sell this and become rich!"
I turned toward her.
She was currently drinking the healing water directly from the fountain.
"Hmm... right."
I looked toward the Mana Well and the Healing Spring.
Both of them had tremendous potential.
"Fine, we’ll do it. But first we need to check the production rate. It doesn’t seem infinite."
I nodded while explaining.
Aurielle happily hugged me in response.
"Feels good" I muttered as her breast directly touched my chest.
Aurielle smiled mischievously before moving even closer and then she used her hands to touch my little brother.
"Damn, you’re in a good mood," I said as I kissed her.
Meanwhile, Aurora watched her master and his crazy wife fooling around together.
For some reason, the atmosphere made her body feel strangely warm.
Then she muttered in a very low voice.
"I want to do that as well."
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Those Who Chose to Stay
paragraphs: Finally, after spending some time playing in the Healing Spring, we came out.
"Aurielle, summon everyone who is loyal to the territory and close to the mansion. Then they will take an oath."
I told Aurielle my idea. After that, we could allow them to enter the Time Chamber and train the knights and mages much faster.
"Okay."
She nodded without hesitation.
We left the secret room together. As I turned back, I noticed the door’s black color gradually fading away until it became almost identical to the surrounding wall once again.
"Good," I muttered.
Soon, we reached the training ground, and Aurielle immediately ordered the maids to summon everyone.
While we waited, many guards and maids quietly discussed among themselves.
"Do you think the lord is going to do something related to the previous rebellion?"
"I don’t know, but I’m afraid. I have a child to feed. I can’t lose this job."
"You’re worrying too much. Maybe the lord wants to reward those who were brave during the fight."
As more and more people arrived, the voices inside the ground gradually became louder.
Even my mages were present. Although they weren’t combat mages and mainly served in support roles, they could still learn new spells, and increasing their ranks would definitely help them greatly.
After waiting for nearly an hour, everyone who was available inside the territory and considered loyal had finally gathered.
The spacious training ground was now filled with guards, maids, servants, and mages.
Aurielle stepped forward.
The moment she moved, everyone straightened instinctively.
Raising her voice with mana, she spoke clearly.
"Thank you for coming here today. Many of you already know me, but some of you may not, so I will introduce myself first."
As she said that, several people focused their attention on her.
Many of them had only heard stories about the young exiled princess who ruled Blackstone Highlands but had never actually seen her in person.
"I am Aurielle Valmont, daughter of the Human Emperor and the Lord of Blackstone Highlands."
She paused slightly as her gaze swept across the crowd.
Then her eyes landed on me, and a small smile appeared on her face.
Raising her hand, she pointed directly toward me.
"He is my husband, Luke Voidheart, the hero summoned by the Goddess of Light herself."
I froze.
I hadn’t expected her to introduce me so suddenly.
Immediately, countless eyes turned toward me.
Whispers spread throughout the crowd.
Many people stared curiously, while others muttered among themselves.
I even heard a few voices.
"Talentless hero?"
Aurielle ignored every whisper.
Instead, her voice became even louder.
"From this day onward, my husband, Luke Voidheart, will become the new Lord of Blackstone Highlands."
Her words echoed through the training hall.
"From now on, everyone will address him as Lord."
Silence.
The entire training ground fell completely silent.
Nobody had expected such an announcement.
Many people simply stared at me with their mouths hanging open.
My mages, however, looked toward me with obvious respect.
I then glanced toward Aurora.
As expected, her expression seemed wrong again.
She looked as if she were witnessing the ascension of a divine being.
In her eyes, I probably had already become someone destined to rule the world.
*"Aurora, don’t go that far..."*
I hurriedly stopped her imagination before she somehow promoted me from territorial lord to ruler of the universe.
"My lady, but—"
The financial advisor finally stepped forward and tried to say something.
However, Aurielle raised her hand and stopped him immediately.
Then she looked toward everyone and spoke in a firm voice.
"I believe in my husband."
Her words carried absolute confidence.
"I believe that with him ruling this territory, we can become greater than before and rise higher than ever."
She paused and carefully observed everyone’s expressions.
Then she finally revealed the most important part.
"Those who are not satisfied are free to leave."
A wave of surprise spread through the crowd.
"I will not stop anyone."
Her voice remained calm.
"Because those who choose to stay here will have to take an oath."
An invisible pressure seemed to settle over the hall.
"A binding oath."
"One that cannot be broken."
After saying that, she fell silent and waited for their response.
Five minutes passed.
Finally, one guard stepped forward.
He knelt on one knee and lowered his head.
"Forgive me, my lord, but I don’t think I can stay in this territory any longer."
Aurielle remained silent and allowed him to continue.
"Many guards are already dead, and I’ve heard about the turmoil at the border."
The moment he mentioned the border, numerous guards and maids visibly stiffened.
Clearly, they had heard the rumors as well.
"I don’t think this territory can survive the problems that are coming."
Then he paused for a moment and glanced toward me before speaking his final concern.
"And I don’t want to lose my life in the war that Viscount Ashenford will bring.
The hall exploded.
"What?!"
"Viscount Ashenford is attacking?"
"Doesn’t that mean we’re doomed?"
Voices rose from every direction.
People began talking anxiously among themselves.
Fear quickly spread through the crowd.
Soon, more guards and maids stepped forward.
One after another, they knelt and requested permission to leave.
Throughout everything, Aurielle remained calm.
Her expression never changed.
It was as if nothing in the world mattered more than making her husband the new lord.
"Okay."
The moment those words left her mouth, the people kneeling visibly relaxed.
"Thank you, my lord."
They bowed gratefully before leaving the training ground one after another.
They weren’t just leaving the hall.
They were abandoning the territory itself.
After they were gone, I looked around.
Only twenty maids remained out of the original fifty.
Among the guards, only ten Iron Knights remained.
The ten Iron Knights who had been guarding the treasury were also present now.
Alongside them stood one hundred Body Tempering Realm soldiers.
Osric, the Bronze Knight, remained as well.
Surprisingly, even the financial advisor had chosen to stay.
"Good."
Aurielle looked satisfied.
Then she turned toward me.
I immediately understood what she wanted.
Walking forward, I stood beside her and gently held her hand.
Then I smiled at everyone who had chosen to remain.
"LORD!"
The remaining people immediately knelt and shouted in unison.
Their voices echoed throughout the training hall.
I nodded toward them.
Then I looked toward Aurora.
"Aurora, come forward."
"Yes, Master."
Aurora stepped out from the behind and walked to the front.
Her silver-white hair swayed softly behind her, while her black-silver armor reflected the light of the sun.
The moment she stopped beside me, confusion appeared on many faces.
Everyone looked curiously at the beautiful knight standing before them.
None of them knew what was about to happen next.
Aurora stepped forward.
Her silver-white hair swayed gently behind her as the runes engraved upon her armor emitted a faint glow.
Though she spoke no words, a strange solemnity spread across the training ground.
One by one, the voices around her disappeared.
Within moments, the entire training ground fell silent.
Then she planted her shield into the ground.
THUD.
A faint silver glow spread beneath her feet.
Then she raised her sword toward the sky.
Her silver-blue eyes shone with an otherworldly radiance as her voice echoed across the entire courtyard.
"Hear me."
"Before steel."
"Before blood."
"Before the witness of heaven and earth."
"I, Aurora Valcrest, invoke the Argent Covenant."
The air suddenly grew heavy.
Countless silver runes appeared around her body.
Then—
CLANG.
CLANG.
CLANG.
Chains began emerging from the empty air.
Everyone watched in shock as a gigantic phantom sword slowly appeared behind Aurora.
The sword was hundreds of meters tall.
Ancient.
Majestic.
Wrapped entirely in countless silver chains.
Its tip pointed toward the heavens.
Its hilt vanished into the sky itself.
The sight alone made many people instinctively lower their heads.
Aurora’s voice rang out once more.
"Those who accept this covenant shall become loyal retainers of Lord Luke Voidheart and the Blackstone Highlands."
"You shall not knowingly betray his trust."
"You shall not raise your blade against him."
"You shall not conspire against his territory.
"And should your heart stray toward betrayal..."
Aurora slowly lowered her sword.
The phantom sword behind her trembled.
The chains wrapped around it rattled violently.
CLANG.
CLANG.
CLANG.
"...then the covenant shall bear witness."
"And the judgment of my sword shall find you."
Silence followed.
The pressure alone made several people struggle to breathe.
Then Aurora spoke the final words.
"Those willing to swear."
"Speak your answer."
The remaining guards, maids, mages, and knights exchanged glances.
Then one by one—
"We swear."
"We swear loyalty to Lord Luke Voidheart."
"We swear loyalty to Blackstone Highlands."
The moment the words left their mouths—
BOOM.
The gigantic phantom sword behind Aurora shone brilliantly.
The chains binding it suddenly burst outward.
Tens of silver chains shot across the training ground.
Like living serpents, they wrapped around every person who had accepted the oath.
The chains glowed for a brief moment.
Then dissolved into countless particles of silver light.
Each person’s chest gained a faint silver covenant mark before it vanished beneath their skin.
The covenant was complete.
Aurielle and I both smiled at this, then we brought them toward the Time Chamber.
As we entered the black tunnel, many people became nervous. Some hesitated for a moment while staring into the darkness ahead, but they still obeyed and followed us inside.
The moment everyone emerged from the tunnel and entered the small world beyond, astonished voices immediately rang out.
"Wow... so much mana!"
Everyone exclaimed in shock.
It seemed that because of the time difference, the Mana Well had already spent quite some time enriching the surrounding environment.
The mana density inside the chamber was noticeably higher than before.
I stepped forward and turned toward my subjects.
They immediately focused their attention on me.
"This is the Time Chamber."
My voice echoed across the open field.
"Here, thirty days are equal to only one day outside."
The moment those words left my mouth, everyone’s expressions froze.
Many people widened their eyes in disbelief.
Time-related treasures were things they had only heard about in stories and legends.
None of them had ever imagined they would stand inside one themselves.
I continued before they could recover from the shock.
"There is also a Mana Well and a Healing Spring."
I pointed toward the distant structures.
"The Mana Well increases the concentration of mana in the surrounding area, while the Healing Spring can heal injuries, restore stamina, and remove fatigue."
I paused and observed their reactions.
Their expressions had completely changed.
The excitement in their eyes was almost frightening.
Many of them immediately began imagining how much stronger they could become by training here.
Soon, whispers began spreading through the crowd.
"If those people knew what they just missed, how much would they regret it?"
"Heh... don’t talk about them. Those guys are traitors."
"They thought this territory was doomed, but our lord will definitely bring back its glory."
Hearing their conversations, I couldn’t help but smile slightly.
Then I raised my voice again.
"Remember."
Everyone immediately turned toward me.
"Do not go near the Mana Well."
"And don’t even think about bathing in the Healing Spring."
The moment I said that, many people instantly looked away.
Several necks visibly shrank.
Even some of the female maids gave me pleading looks, as if I had just exposed exactly what they had been planning to do.
I had seen better than that.
So I didn’t melt under their pitiful expressions.
After giving everyone a few more instructions, we left them inside the Time Chamber.
Only the Financial Advisor, Aurora, Aurielle, and I returned outside.
There were still many things we needed to discuss regarding the territory’s future.
And now that we finally had loyal people and resources...
It was time to begin our next plan.
[Chapter End]
