chapters.title: Chapter 24: No Mercy for Parasites
paragraphs: As we left the treasury and moved through the hallways, I noticed Margaret standing quietly to the side.
I slowed my pace slightly before calling her over in a low voice.
Margaret looked at me with confusion before approaching.
Leaning closer to her ear, I lowered my voice and gave Aurielle a brief glance.
"Margaret, did you notice that Aurielle seems a little different after yesterday’s incident?"
She blinked and gave me a puzzled look.
"She seems more possessive."
Her confusion only deepened.
After all, she had been with Aurielle since she woke up and hadn’t noticed anything particularly unusual.
"Nothing, my lord..."
She paused midway through her sentence as if suddenly remembering something.
"But I heard that the Silver Knight of Ashenford said you were dead. Only after hearing that did everything happen, and she lost consciousness."
She finished speaking and gave me a meaningful look.
"You should take better care of her, my lord. It seems she was deeply shocked by that."
I nodded lightly.
"Thanks."
With that, I quickened my pace and caught up with everyone.
After reaching the meeting room, we each took our seats.
Aurielle personally guided me toward the main seat before settling down on my right.
Aurora silently took her place behind me like an unwavering guardian.
The room gradually fell silent.
I looked around the table before taking out a sheet of paper.
"I toured the territory and identified several major problems."
My gaze swept across everyone present.
"If anyone has suggestions, feel free to speak."
Osric and Aurielle both nodded.
Finally, my eyes landed on the old man sitting nearby.
Edmund Blackwell.
Chief Financial Advisor of Blackstone Highlands.
A veteran administrator who had served the territory for many years.
Known for his strict budgeting, terrifying accuracy with numbers.
Despite his stern appearance, he genuinely cared for the people and remained one of Aurielle’s most trusted retainers.
Edmund slowly raised a hand.
I nodded.
"My lord, Baron Cedric has closed the river again with his dam."
His voice carried obvious anger.
"And it seems he has no intention of opening it this time."
The moment those words left his mouth, the atmosphere in the room became heavy.
Everyone’s expressions darkened.
Baron Cedric had done this many times before, and every time it created enormous difficulties for the territory.
Even Aurielle’s expression became unpleasant.
Seeing the mood sink, I calmly spoke.
"I’ve already dealt with the water problem for the territory. You don’t need to worry about it for at least a month."
"What?"
Everyone immediately stood up.
Shock filled their faces.
Aurielle merely smiled slightly.
I took out the Aqua Crystals and placed them on the table.
"You can also use these to refill wells and ponds throughout the territory."
I handed one crystal each to Osric, Edmund, and Aurielle.
The tension in the room instantly eased.
Relief appeared on their faces.
They sat back down.
"I’ve also dealt with the food problem for now."
I then explained the Mana Wheat Seeds.
By the time I finished, everyone was staring at me with speechless expressions.
It was as if they couldn’t believe that I had become lord only recently and had already solved two of the territory’s biggest problems.
I ignored their looks and continued.
"Now, another problem is unemployment and insecurity among our people."
The moment those words left my mouth, everyone’s expressions changed.
Several people clenched their fists.
Edmund sighed heavily before speaking.
"My lord, forgive me, but our territory has nearly five thousand poor civilians who mainly depend on farming."
He paused before continuing.
"We tried giving work to the adults before so they could support their families, but..."
His voice trailed off.
A struggling expression appeared on his face.
He couldn’t bring himself to finish.
I was about to urge him to continue when Aurielle spoke first.
"Edmund. Tell us."
Her voice was firm.
Edmund visibly flinched.
After taking a deep breath, he finally nodded.
"After your mother left, there was no one capable of properly governing the territory."
"Although I managed the finances and prevented excessive waste, Lady Evelyne—your aunt—was responsible for worker management, money distribution, and territory maintenance."
He paused briefly before continuing.
"But she never actually used the funds to repair the territory."
His expression darkened.
"Together with Roland, she frequently traveled to other cities to indulge in pleasure."
"As a result, enormous amounts of gold were wasted."
The room fell silent.
I looked toward Aurielle.
Disgust and displeasure were written all over her face.
BANG!
Her palm slammed heavily onto the table.
Edmund jumped slightly.
"Where is she?"
Aurielle’s voice had become ice cold.
Edmund answered nervously.
"My lord... she isn’t in the territory right now."
"She left for another city before you returned."
I placed a hand on Aurielle’s shoulder.
Her anger eased slightly.
Then I looked toward Edmund.
"Any other immediate problems?"
He nodded.
"Yes, my lord."
His expression became grim.
"There is the Blackstone Jackals gang."
"The gang has been terrorizing the people for years."
"They are responsible for many crimes throughout the territory."
He began listing them.
• Protection fees from vendors
• Illegal gambling
• Smuggling
• Extorting travelers
• Loan sharking
• Theft
The moment Aurielle and I heard that list, my face darkened.
I turned toward Osric.
He simply nodded.
Clearly, he already knew.
"Then why haven’t they been punished or imprisoned?"
My voice carried obvious anger.
Both Edmund and Osric visibly flinched.
Osric lowered his head before answering.
"My lord, it’s not that I never tried."
"Their leader is a Bronze Realm Knight."
"He also has several Iron Knights among his members."
I frowned.
"That doesn’t sound like a local gang."
"They sound more like a private army."
Osric nodded.
"Yes, my lord."
"There is definitely a noble supporting them from behind the scenes."
"We simply don’t know who."
"Lady Evelyne never ordered us to deal with them, and Roland, as vice captain, also chose to do nothing."
When he finally finished speaking, I slowly took a deep breath.
The room fell silent.
THUD.
I rose from my seat.
"Good."
A cold smile slowly appeared on my face.
Aurielle, Edmund, and Osric all looked at me.
Without another word, I began walking toward the door.
Aurora immediately followed behind me.
Confusion appeared on everyone’s faces.
Only Aurielle seemed to understand what was about to happen.
Then my voice echoed through the room.
"Osric."
"Order the one hundred Iron Knights and ten Bronze Knights of my Blackstone Legion to assemble."
The moment he heard that, Osric became visibly nervous.
"My lord, but what about the noble backing them?"
I stopped.
Slowly turning back, I looked directly at him.
Then a cold smile appeared on my face.
"To hell with them."
The temperature in the room seemed to drop.
"This is my territory."
"If they set foot here, then they follow my rules."
I paused.
My eyes became cold.
"Otherwise..."
"I’ll destroy them."
CREEEEAK.
The meeting room door slowly opened.
Without looking back again, I stepped outside.
Aurora followed silently behind me.
A second later, Osric hurriedly stood up and began issuing orders to the servants.
The Blackstone Legion was about to move.
[Chapter End]

A cold smile slowly appeared on my face.
Aurielle, Edmund, and Osric all looked at me.
Without another word, I began walking toward the door.
Aurora immediately followed behind me.
Confusion appeared on everyone’s faces.
Only Aurielle seemed to understand what was about to happen.
Then my voice echoed through the room.
"Osric."
"Order the one hundred Iron Knights and ten Bronze Knights of my Blackstone Legion to assemble."
The moment he heard that, Osric became visibly nervous.
"My lord, but what about the noble backing them?"
I stopped.
Slowly turning back, I looked directly at him.
Then a cold smile appeared on my face.
"To hell with them."
The temperature in the room seemed to drop.
"This is my territory."
"If they set foot here, then they follow my rules."
I paused.
My eyes became cold.
"Otherwise..."
"I’ll destroy them."
CREEEEAK.
The meeting room door slowly opened.
Without looking back again, I stepped outside.
Aurora followed silently behind me.
A second later, Osric hurriedly stood up and began issuing orders to the servants.
The Blackstone Legion was about to move.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 25: Wrath of the New Lord
paragraphs: As I reached the main gate area, I found more than a hundred knights standing in formation alongside ten Bronze Knights.
Their backs were straight, hands resting on their weapons, and every face carried a serious expression. They looked like a wall of steel standing before the estate.
Anyone foolish enough to stand against them would regret it.

I also noticed several guards and maids who had no interest in staying within the territory and were preparing to leave. They were carrying bags and small bundles of belongings, but the moment they saw the assembled force, they paused and stared.
Their eyes widened as they looked at the ranks of armored knights gathered beneath the Blackstone banner.
I stepped forward and raised my voice.
"Warriors, prepare. Today, we are going to remove the pests from our land."
My gaze swept across the formation.
"The same land where our families live."
"The same land where our children grow up."
THUD.
Every knight struck a fist against their chest armor.
"AS YOU COMMAND, MY LORD!!!"
Their voices exploded outward and echoed throughout the entrance area.
Several maids flinched in surprise.
Even the departing guards looked stunned by the sheer unity in the knights’ response.
I turned and began walking toward the main gate.
Without hesitation, the knights followed behind me.
STEP.
STEP.
STEP.
Hundreds of synchronized footsteps echoed across the stone road as we left the lord’s estate.
The sound was heavy and rhythmic, causing nearby servants to instinctively move aside.
Dust rose lightly beneath the marching formation while the Blackstone banner fluttered above us in the morning breeze.
After traveling for some time, we entered the market district.
The streets were crowded as usual.
Merchants pushed wagons loaded with goods.
Vendors shouted to attract customers.
Children ran between stalls while adventurers and travelers moved through the busy streets.
However, the moment people noticed more than a hundred armored knights marching through the district, the atmosphere gradually changed.
Conversations slowed.
Merchants stopped arranging their goods.
Customers paused in the middle of bargaining.
Many people stepped aside to clear a path as we advanced.
Curious gazes followed our every movement.
"What’s happening?"
"Why are so many knights here?"
"Did something happen?"
Whispers spread through the market as more and more people turned their attention toward us.
Although they looked nervous, curiosity quickly overcame their fear.
One by one, people began following behind our group to see where we were going.
I didn’t stop them.
After nearly two minutes of walking, we finally arrived in front of a large pub.
People continuously entered and exited through its doors. Some were merchants taking a break from work, while others were adventurers enjoying a drink after finishing commissions.
Then I looked toward Osric.
Besides the knights, he was the only person I had brought with me.
Osric looked at the building before giving a grim nod.
"Yes, my lord. This is one of their main gathering locations."
The moment people entering and leaving the pub noticed us—and the growing crowd following behind us—they immediately stopped.
Confused whispers began spreading through the area.
"What are they doing here?"
"Do you think they’re finally going after the Blackstone Jackals?"
"What are you talking about? I heard the lord is useless. She never dared to touch them."
"Your information is outdated."
Another person quickly interrupted.
"I heard a new lord appeared and was personally chosen by the exiled princess."
He pointed toward me.
"Look at the front. That black-haired guy is supposed to be the new lord."
Immediately, dozens of eyes landed on me.
Some carried doubt.
Others carried curiosity.
But among the commoners, there was something else, Hope.
Several vendors exchanged glances.
A vegetable seller tightened her grip on the basket in her hands.
"Do you really think they’re going to punish them this time?"
Her voice trembled slightly.
Before anyone could answer, another voice suddenly spoke.
"They sold my son."
The surrounding chatter gradually died down.
A thin middle-aged man stepped forward.
His clothes were old and worn, and his face looked malnourished from years of hardship.
Tears slowly gathered in his eyes.
"They took my daughter too."
His voice cracked.
"I complained day and night."
"I reported it everywhere I could."
"But nobody listened to me."
Silence spread through the crowd.
Several people lowered their heads.
Others clenched their fists.
A few stepped forward and gently patted the man’s shoulder.
Nobody laughed, Nobody mocked him.
Because everyone knew he wasn’t the only victim.
Osric heard those words.
And so did I.
My expression remained unchanged, but the anger inside me grew even colder.
"Surround the pub. I don’t want anyone escaping."
I ordered my knights, and they instantly moved into action.
The formation split apart as armored knights rushed in every direction, quickly surrounding the entire building.
Those who were about to enter immediately stopped and backed away when they saw rows of drawn swords blocking every exit.
The atmosphere around the pub instantly became tense.
Meanwhile, a man with a jackal tattoo on his neck happened to glance out from a second-floor window.
The moment he saw knights surrounding the building from every side, his expression changed.
Cold sweat appeared on his forehead.
"Boss! We have a problem!"
He shouted before turning around and running toward the leader’s room.
Inside the room, a burly man was playing cards with several other hooligans while some drank loudly and others chatted around the tables.
Laughter and the sound of clinking mugs filled the room.
The moment they saw the man’s panicked expression, the noise gradually died down.
Several gang members looked up.
Others frowned.
"What happened?"
The boss lowered the cards in his hand and fixed the man with a sharp gaze.
The man took several rough breaths before shouting loudly,
"Boss! We’ve been surrounded by knights! I also heard them talking about some new lord!"
The boss’s hands stopped moving.
A dangerous look appeared in his eyes as he stared at the panicked man.
However, before he could say anything—
BANG!
A deafening explosion echoed throughout the building.
The front entrance burst open.
The sound shook the entire pub.
Several mugs fell from tables.
Customers jumped from their seats in shock.
"What the hell?!"
Everyone immediately stood up.
Some gang members grabbed their weapons while others hurried toward the stairs.
At the same time, I lowered my leg after kicking the door open and stepped inside.
The interior of the pub was far larger than it appeared from outside.
Rows of tables filled the hall.
Customers occupied nearly every corner.
Waitresses dressed in revealing clothing moved between tables carrying drinks.
The place was large enough to accommodate hundreds of people.
Then they saw us.
Hundreds of armored knights entered behind me with weapons in hand.
The metallic sound of armor echoed throughout the hall.
Clang.
Clang.
Clang.
The atmosphere instantly changed.
The laughter disappeared and the conversations stopped.
Even the drunkest customers suddenly looked sober.
I swept my gaze across the room before speaking.
"Everyone who is not a member of the Blackstone Jackals..."
My voice echoed through the hall.
"Leave. Now."
For a moment, nobody moved.
Many simply stared at us in shock.
Then several knights stepped forward with their swords drawn.
SHING!
The sharp sound finally snapped everyone awake and panic erupted.
People rushed toward the entrance.
Chairs overturned and tables were pushed aside.
Several customers nearly tripped over each other while trying to escape.
"Don’t do anything to us! We’re not members of that gang!"
People screamed and begged as they ran toward the exit.
I didn’t stop them.
Every gang member carried a jackal tattoo on their neck.
There was no need.
Soon, only the gang members remained inside.
STEP.
STEP.
STEP.
Heavy footsteps echoed from the upper floor.
More than fifty men emerged with murderous expressions on their faces.
I looked toward their necks.
Each one carried a different colored jackal tattoo.
Some held swords. Others carried axes and clubs.
A bald man stepped forward first.
"We always paid money to the territory."
His eyes narrowed.
"Then why have you come today with this force?"
I didn’t answer.
Instead, I waited until the last civilian left the building.
At that moment, my knights already had their swords pointed toward the gang members.
Seeing that I completely ignored him, the bald man’s expression darkened.
Then a larger figure stepped forward from behind him.
A burly man with a bronze jackal tattoo on his neck.
The leader.
"You seem to be the new lord people have been talking about."
He studied me while observing the surrounding knights.
"Seems like he can’t sense their aura," I thought as I noticed him releasing his Mid Bronze Realm aura.
A wave of pressure spread from his body, causing several gang members to smirk proudly.
Then he spoke again.
"If my lord finds out that you’re disrupting his business, he will be very angry."
His voice carried an obvious threat.
"And if he gets angry..."
A cruel smile appeared on his face.
"You can forget about this little territory of yours."
I looked at him for a moment before speaking.
"Kill them."
My order was calm and straightforward.
Since all the civilians had already left the building, there was no reason to wait any longer.
The gang members blinked in confusion.
Many looked at each other in disbelief.
"Didn’t he hear what our boss just said?"
That thought appeared in almost every mind.
Then—
BOOOOOOM!
A terrifying pressure exploded throughout the pub.
Every knight released their aura.
The air itself seemed to become heavier.
Several gang members immediately staggered backward.
The confidence on their faces vanished.
Fear quickly replaced it.
Because they could finally sense the strength standing before them.
Ten Peak Bronze Knights.
Hundreds of Peak Iron Knights.
The overwhelming difference nearly crushed their spirits.
Some people’s legs immediately began trembling.
Others subconsciously stepped backward.
Several even dropped their weapons.
CLANG.
CLANG.
The sound of steel hitting the floor echoed throughout the hall.
STEP.
The knights took a single step forward.
That simple movement completely shattered the remaining courage of the gang members.
Many stumbled backward and fell onto their knees.
"My lord!"
"Please forgive us!"
"We surrender!"
"Don’t kill us!"
Almost more than half the gang members immediately began begging for their lives.
Some lowered their heads.
Others looked ready to cry.
Even the leader’s expression became extremely ugly.
He lowered his voice and spoke to the members closest to him.
"We have to escape."
His trusted subordinates instantly understood.
"We return to our lord."
"He’ll deal with this."
BANG!
The moment he finished speaking, he exploded into motion.
The stairs shattered beneath his feet as he rushed toward the upper floor.
Wood fragments scattered everywhere.
Several gang members followed him toward the stairs while others rushed toward nearby windows.
BOOM!
BOOM!
But the knights moved as well.
Five Peak Bronze Knights instantly leaped upward.
The upper floor exploded under the impact.
Wood splintered and support beams cracked.
Dust filled the air.
THUD!
The leader dropped back down from above.
"WAIT!"
He shouted desperately.
Unfortunately for him—
SHING!
More than five swords pierced through his body at the same time.
His eyes widened as blood flowed from his mouth.
Then the light gradually faded from his eyes.
THUD.
His corpse collapsed onto the floor.
The remaining gang members froze.
Panic spread through their ranks.
Any remaining thoughts of resistance disappeared.
One by one, every fleeing member was hunted down and killed.
The sounds of battle echoed throughout the pub.
Clang!
Shing!
Boom!
Screams mixed with the sound of steel.
Yet the fight ended almost as quickly as it had begun.
Soon silence returned.
THUD.
A Bronze Knight knelt before me.
"My lord."
"What should we do with the remaining members?"
The surviving gang members immediately looked toward me.
Their faces were filled with fear and several had tears in their eyes, while others looked completely defeated.
I narrowed my eyes before giving my order.
"Destroy their Aether Seeds."
The remaining prisoners instantly went pale.
Then I added,
"And take them away."
"We need more prisoners for the mines."
The expressions of the surviving gang members changed completely.
Destroying an Aether Seed wasn’t death.
But for knights, it was often worse.
Years of training.
Years of effort.
Years of sacrifice.
All erased in an instant.
Their future path would end here.
Yet despite the despair in their eyes, none of them dared resist.
Outside, people were gathered around the pub, waiting nervously for the outcome.
"Do you think those gang members will just bribe them and get away again?"
One vendor asked quietly.
The man beside him shook his head.
"Doesn’t seem like it. Otherwise, the lord wouldn’t have brought this many knights."
BOOM!
BANG!
BOOM!
As they were talking, loud sounds suddenly echoed from inside the building.
Everyone immediately stopped speaking.
Several people instinctively stepped back.
Others stared at the entrance without blinking.
A few minutes later, the doors finally opened.
Hundreds of knights marched out.
At the very front stood the new lord.
Many people looked around in confusion.
"Where are the gang members?"
However, their doubts were answered almost immediately.
Corpses began appearing behind the knights.
One after another.
All of them carried jackal tattoos on their necks.
Behind the corpses came dozens of gang members bound with ropes.
Blood leaked from the corners of many mouths.
Several looked completely defeated.
The crowd fell silent.
"They really took out the gang."
Someone muttered in disbelief.
Another person stared at the prisoners.
"Does this mean the Blackstone Jackals are finished?"
Many people felt their eyes becoming moist as they looked at the corpses and prisoners.
For years, these criminals had terrorized the territory.
And now they were gone.
I looked toward the crowd and stopped walking.
The knights behind me also came to a halt.
I raised my voice with mana and spoke loudly.
"I am Luke Voidheart."
"The Lord of Blackstone Highlands."
"And the husband of Aurielle Valmont."
The crowd immediately became silent.
Everyone looked toward me with serious expressions.
I continued.
"THIS IS MY TERRITORY."
My voice echoed throughout the market.
"IF YOU WANT TO LIVE HERE..."
"IF YOU WANT TO DO BUSINESS HERE..."
"THEN DO SO FREELY."
I paused briefly before my expression turned colder.
"BUT IF ANYONE DARES TO BREAK THE LAW..."
"IF ANYONE DARES TO PREY UPON MY PEOPLE..."
"THEN THEY WILL FACE MY WRATH."
Many people unconsciously looked toward the prisoners behind me.
I lowered my voice slightly before adding,
"From today onward, there are no more Blackstone Jackals."
"You no longer need to pay unnecessary protection fees."
"You no longer need to fear harassment."
"You no longer need to bow your heads before criminals."
As I observed the crowd, I noticed many people’s eyes becoming red.
Several merchants smiled in relief.
Even adventurers looked visibly satisfied.
For the first time in years, they no longer had to worry about the gang’s oppression.
Then suddenly—
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
A voice erupted from somewhere within the crowd.
Nobody knew who started it.
But another voice quickly followed.
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
Then another.
And another.
Soon the entire area was filled with cheers.
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
The sound echoed throughout the market.
People raised their fists.
Merchants shouted loudly.
Even several children joined the cheering.
I nodded slightly with a faint smile.
Then I turned around and began walking back toward the lord’s estate.
The knights immediately followed behind me.
As we moved forward, the crowd naturally stepped aside.
A long path opened before us.
People stood on both sides of the road, watching us pass.
Some cheered while some bowed.
Others simply looked on with admiration.
For a brief moment, it almost felt like a victorious king returning from battle.
[Chapter End]

The crowd immediately became silent.
Everyone looked toward me with serious expressions.
I continued.
"THIS IS MY TERRITORY."
My voice echoed throughout the market.
"IF YOU WANT TO LIVE HERE..."
"IF YOU WANT TO DO BUSINESS HERE..."
"THEN DO SO FREELY."
I paused briefly before my expression turned colder.
"BUT IF ANYONE DARES TO BREAK THE LAW..."
"IF ANYONE DARES TO PREY UPON MY PEOPLE..."
"THEN THEY WILL FACE MY WRATH."
Many people unconsciously looked toward the prisoners behind me.
I lowered my voice slightly before adding,
"From today onward, there are no more Blackstone Jackals."
"You no longer need to pay unnecessary protection fees."
"You no longer need to fear harassment."
"You no longer need to bow your heads before criminals."
As I observed the crowd, I noticed many people’s eyes becoming red.
Several merchants smiled in relief.
Even adventurers looked visibly satisfied.
For the first time in years, they no longer had to worry about the gang’s oppression.
Then suddenly—
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
A voice erupted from somewhere within the crowd.
Nobody knew who started it.
But another voice quickly followed.
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
Then another.
And another.
Soon the entire area was filled with cheers.
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
"LONG LIVE THE LORD!"
The sound echoed throughout the market.
People raised their fists.
Merchants shouted loudly.
Even several children joined the cheering.
I nodded slightly with a faint smile.
Then I turned around and began walking back toward the lord’s estate.
The knights immediately followed behind me.
As we moved forward, the crowd naturally stepped aside.
A long path opened before us.
People stood on both sides of the road, watching us pass.
Some cheered while some bowed.
Others simply looked on with admiration.
For a brief moment, it almost felt like a victorious king returning from battle.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 26: The Possessive Wife
paragraphs: Ashenford Territory:
A brown-haired man seated on a throne asked the kneeling person,
"Any message come from Roland or Darius?"
The kneeling man is wearing full-body black clothes that are used for hiding and stealth.
"No, my lord."
He paused slightly after saying this and told him about the information he found out.
"I have heard from the people who left the mansion that the Ashenford army did attack the mansion and almost completely took it down."
He paused for breath, then continued.
"But the husband of the exiled princess suddenly brought a thousand-person army and took it back."
"After defeating the Ashenford army, they released the news that their army, along with Roland and the Silver Knight, suddenly disappeared."
BANG
The armrest of the throne shattered as the person shouted furiously.
"What do you mean they just disappeared?!"
"They have clearly killed all of them!"
His face became angry because not only had he lost his son, but his brother as well, who was a Peak Silver Knight.
"My lord, should we attack the territory then?"
The kneeling person asked, who is affected by the man’s pressure as well, but still didn’t move.
The Ashenford Lord paused and started thinking.
After a moment, he shook his head.
"No, we can’t."
He looked at the kneeling man and sighed as he said,
"Count’s daughter’s birthday is here, and I am sure he will send invitations to everyone."
He gritted his teeth and said in a heavy voice,
"Even though I want to kill them, if the Count finds out that I attacked his invited people, he will surely take my head instead."
He took a deep breath to calm down, but the next moment his smile became sinister.
"We will deal with their territory after the event, but if some assassin kills the territory owner, then what can I do?"
"Hahahhah."
"Go, give those assassins the commission."
He said while laughing.
The kneeling man nodded, then disappeared.
After returning, I met Elmund, who is shocked by the gathering crowd, as many people have come to see us off and are now standing in front of the Lord’s estate gate.
"My Lord, is everything alright?"
He asked me worriedly, on which I smiled and told him the news of the Blackstone Jackals’ extermination.
He got surprised that I have finished it so quickly.
Then I gave him two pouches of gold coins, on which a shocked expression came onto his face.
"This?"
He asked confusedly.
I told him to gather the people of this territory and give jobs to all of them who wanted to earn some money for themselves and their families.
"Also add that we are going to give them two meals and ten copper coins per day."
As he listened to my words, his face changed instantly as he immediately bowed down.
"My Lord, the territory is blessed that we have got you and Miss Aurielle."
He cried while saying this.
The surrounding guards and maids also looked emotional because now the citizens didn’t have to go to sleep on an empty stomach, as they had faced that once as well.
"It’s fine."
I waved my hand at him, then started walking toward the mansion for lunch.
"Aurielle."
After reaching the dining room, I sat at the main seat as she was already seated on my right.
She gave me a loving smile while saying,
"You have done a good job, husband."
After that, we started eating.
Aurora was not here, as she is guarding the mage.
I shook my head to remove these thoughts and told Aurielle about my next plan.
"Aurielle, I am going to clear the nearest bandit group this afternoon and try to return before night."
She paused slightly, then looked at me with resentment because after waking up, I hadn’t been able to give her proper time.
"Do you really have to go?"
She asked as she stood up from her seat, came behind me, and hugged me.
I held her hand and replied in a calming voice,
"Don’t worry. After returning, I will give you all the time you want."
Finally, her expression eased slightly, but she didn’t return to her seat.
Instead—
"Ahhh."
She sat on my lap and opened her mouth wide for food.
I laughed slowly at her childish behavior but obliged.
"Mhhmmm."
She ate with a smile.
As we continued eating, I finally heard something good.
[Return System Activated, Target Aurielle]
My hand paused slightly while feeding her, on which she gave me a confused look.
I shook my head and continued feeding her while also listening to the system notification.
[Emotional State: Possessiveness / Jealousy / Love]
"Wait?? Jealousy?"
I thought about this.
Then Aurora’s figure came into my mind and her reaction.
A small smile appeared on my lips.
"Why are you grinning like an idiot?"
Suddenly, I heard Aurielle’s voice as she asked after noticing my smile.
Before I could answer, she continued.
"Don’t tell me, are you thinking about another woman again?"
I gave her a speechless look as she stared at me with suspicious-filled eyes.
"Sometimes trust your innocent husband." Even though I did think about Aurora.
I muttered, then stood up.
She barely managed to stop herself from falling and immediately gave me a glare, as she had already judged me guilty.
"I am resting in my room."
I said to her, who likely wanted to find this mysterious other woman.
"Dealing with one wife is so tension-filled, and I have four other wives as well."
I said with a sigh as I reached my room.
After sitting down, I rubbed my hands together and prayed to the Goddess of Luck with an excited expression before finally checking the system message.
[Milestone Reached: LOVE AND POSSESSIVENESS]
[From now on all the returns from wife Aurielle will start at 100x]
"The hell!"
A curse came out of my mouth as I stood up abruptly.
"100x? Really? This is crazy."
I muttered while getting excited.
Before I could say more, the system’s emotionless voice sounded.
[Luke, don’t be so happy so soon.]
Question marks appeared in my head.
"What do you mean?"
[Well, because that 100x still depends on rewards, so maybe you will just get a silver coin and it will become a hundred silver coins.]
I stopped, sat down, and asked for more explanation.
[Sigh... Luke, rewards depend on many calculations, but mostly on the event that happened and new emotions.]
[So sorry, unless you are the husband of the Goddess of Luck, you can even get a stone.]
"The world looks so lonely."
I muttered as I slumped onto my bed with a lost expression.
But after a few moments, the system motivated me, as it is still 100x and there is even an option to become the husband of the Goddess of Luck as well.
I gave him a deep glare when he mentioned the Goddess of Luck.
Then, with a sigh, I finally checked the rewards.
[Chapter End.]

chapters.title: Chapter 27 - 100x Return: Rise of the Blackstone Legion
paragraphs: DING!
[LOVE AND POSSESSIVENESS Reward Granted]
[100x Return Triggered]
The reward has exceeded its original value.
Path of Ascension Package ×100
Obtained:
10,000 Body Tempering Breakthrough Potions
1,000 Iron Breakthrough Potions
100 Bronze Breakthrough Potions
1,000 Gold Coins
A force capable of producing:
• 10,000 Iron Realm Knights
• 1,000 Bronze Realm Knights
• 100 Silver Realm Knights
[Perfect Realm Stabilization Effect Preserved]
[All Breakthrough Potions Remain 100% Safe]
[Reward Upgraded Successfully]
"Awesome" I blurted out after seeing the insane rewards. But as I remembered system words, my mood calmed down slightly.
"I hope next time stone will not come out" I prayed to goddess of luck, then told the maid to summon everyone in the territory to Time Chamber.
After that I also headed towards it.
As Luke was going alone while singing song, he didn’t know that his order had created mass panic among everyone.
"What’s happened?, will the lord punish us or gonna fire us?"
Many people thought about this, but they still obliged and moved toward the Time Chamber with worried face.
Aurielle, Margaret, Elmund and Osric got confused, still they also followed.
Only mages and Aurora were left alone outside.
Aurora, seeing all this, got down to ground and started drawing circle with a stick while muttering.
"Lord doesn’t want me anymore"
Elena and other mages gave her a weird look, then they settled down and awaited their master.
"Definitely that crazy wife has done something" They completely ignored Aurora’s complaints.
Inside Time Chamber:
I looked toward everyone and nodded, then said with a loud voice.
"I have got some resources, which will allow everyone to reach next realm."
A pin drop silence, because I have said something incredible to all the people present, which is 142 of mansion remaining persons and others are my summon legions.
Even they got shocked.
I ignored their reactions and gave each of them the breakthrough potion.
THUD.
"Thank you lord, for you we are prepard to offer our lives" Everyone knelt together, even maids, then they shouted together to declare their faith.
I looked at everyone’s expressions and can see it. "It is sincere" I nodded, then also gave Elmund, who is still Body Tempering realm, and Osric, who is peak Bronze Knight.
After everyone took their potion, they moved to find suitable locations, as Mana Well has increased mana concentration in whole surrounding.
"I know, its definitely her" Aurielle suddenly came from behind and said in my ear.
"Haha" I laughed and also gave her an Iron Knight breakthrough potion.
She looked at the potion glass vial, which was shimmering with black-silver light, then she leaned and kissed me.
"ahhh" I got surprised, as there are many people, but after a moment she separated and gave me a small wink, before getting close to Mana Well.
"Sigh" I shook my head and headed in the same direction as well.
I settled after finding a good location.
GULP.
Then I gulped down the body temper breakthrough potion in one go.
At first... nothing.
Just a dull heaviness settling in my stomach.
But then—
A faint warmth stirred.
Like a single ember waking up in the depths of my body.
"ahhh."
The whisper escaped my lips without meaning to.
The warmth turned into heat.
Then into burning.
BOOM.
My eyes widened as the potion fully activated.
It isn’t just heat anymore—it is a raging current.
Aether and mana erupted inside me like a storm breaking loose from a sealed dam.
"Ugh—!"
I clenched my jaw as my body jerked forward.
Veins across my arms and neck bulged violently, dark lines glowing faintly as mana flooded through channels that were never meant to handle this much pressure.
Crack... crack...
My bones responded first.
As they start *re-forging*.
Every fracture, every impurity I never knew existed was being forcefully crushed and rebuilt under the potion’s will.
My muscles tightened next.
Fibers twisting, compressing, expanding again—like steel being hammered in a furnace.
My heartbeat thundered in my ears.
THUMP—THUMP—THUMP.
Each pulse pushed more mana through my body.
Head → Heart → Limbs → Dantian.
The circulation instinct I had learned earlier activated on its own.
But this time... it was different.
More faster and more heavier.
Like something inside me was demanding to be come outside.
"My body... is reaching its limit..."
I gritted my teeth as sweat poured down my face.
Then—
Something inside my dantian *collapsed inward*.
The process of compression.
Everything—blood, mana, will, instinct, fighting spirit—was being pulled into a single point.
A tiny and fragile black-silver grain began to form.
But infinitely dense.
"Aether Seed..."
The words surfaced in my mind instinctively.
And the moment it appeared—
BOOM!!
A shockwave erupted through my body.
Every vein lit up.
Every muscle surged.
Every bone vibrated as if answering the Aether seed command.
Pain exploded for a brief instant—
then vanished instantly and replaced by absolute clarity.
My breathing slowed while my heartbeat stabilized.
And the pressure in my body... settled.
The Aether Seed rotated gently in my dantian, like a sleeping sun.
Then—
It pulsed.
WOOOOOM.
A wave of power swept through me, washing over every part of my body.
My skin shed a thin layer of black impurities instantly.
My senses sharpened as my strength multiplied.
My mana circulation stabilized at a completely different level.
I slowly opened my eyes.
A faint silver-black aura flickered around my body before fading into my skin.
"...so this is Iron Knight."
I flexed my fingers. The air around them trembled slightly.
Not because I was releasing power—
but because my body could no longer contain it as before.
A faint smile formed on my lips.
"Finally... I’ve crossed the threshold."
I stood up slowly.
CRACK.
The ground beneath me cracked from a single step.
Again this short term power gain. I shook my head.
Then my gaze sharpened as I looked ahead.
The world felt... lighter and more clearer than before, as I could see the grass clearly and could even hear people’s pained voices as well.
"Seems like many are still in breakthrough process," I muttered as I surveyed my surroundings.
Then I felt somewhere deep inside my dantian—
the Aether Seed pulsed once more.
As if reminding me.
This is only the beginning.
"Good," I smiled.
"Though many people still call it mana, even after the Aether Seed formed," I said while releasing the energy around my body which felt in better control. "I will call it aether from now on."
After that I took a shower in the Healing Spring, as its water cleans itself very fast, then waited for others to complete their breakthrough as well.
BOOM BOOM BOOM.
One by one many auras released throughout the chamber, as finally everyone finished their breakthrough.
"Huh..., all maids have broken through to Iron Knight Realm," I said then calculated.
Now I have Blackstone Legion,
BLACKSTONE LEGION :
1,000 Early Iron Knights
100 Early Bronze Knights
10 Early Silver Knights
1 Peak Silver Knight (Aurora)
Plus those territory guards also ranked up, which will increase the security more.
"Ok everyone, take a short break, then we will clear some bandits who are stopping or harassing the people from coming into our territory."
I said to everyone.
"YES SIR!!!" they replied energetically.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 28: The Land Worth Saving
paragraphs: As we exited the Time Chamber and reached the stable area, my expression became 0-0.
I turned toward Osric, who is looking at the sky, likely enjoying its beauty.
"Where is the horse?" Other guards backed away and dropped everything on Osric’s head, who was now sweating from his head.
"My lord... that..." He said slowly and was struggling to complete his words.
He finally gritted his teeth and said, "My lord, as we don’t use horses, because no guards go out of the territory, Lady Evelyne sold all the horses." He looked down as he was ashamed of this.
"Seriously?" I facepalmed myself and thought, "Now do I need to walk by myself?"
Then—
"My lord, here is your horse." I turned toward the voice and saw Aurora, who was now fully armed, holding the reins of a muscular black horse and smiling brightly at me.
Aurielle also got out with Margaret to see me off, now stunned after seeing this and asked her.
"From where did you get this horse?"
Aurora looked confused at Aurielle, but answered.
"Hmm... I got this from the stable of those bandits that Master took care of."
Hearing this, I turned toward Osric. He nodded and said, "My lord, normally these bases always have loot. It’s just that we count all of it together and then present the report."
My expression finally relaxed after hearing about the loot, then Osric added, "There were around ten horses I saw in that stable."
"Good, ten Early Bronze Knights come with me and take the horses," I said to everyone and reached toward the horse Aurora brought.
"Good girl." I patted her head, on which she giggled like a fangirl.
Then I mounted the horse. Even though I don’t know how to ride properly, I used my aura to suppress it and control it before being able to move some distance.
But as I was about to leave the territory, Aurora started climbing onto the same horse as me.
Then—
"What are you doing?" Aurielle suddenly got behind her in a flash and held her hand while shouting at her behavior.
Aurora looked at me with teary eyes and said, "I want to go with my lord."
"Poor girl," I thought and was about to reply, but Aurielle cut me off.
"No need, he will come back soon. You stay with us," Aurielle said and started dragging her back toward the mansion.
"NO!!! Master, don’t leave me behind with this crazy woman."
Everyone flinched when she said this and then all of them looked at the sky and thought, "Today’s weather is so nice."
I gave one last pitying look toward Aurora, then left the territory with 10 Early Bronze Knights.
As I passed through the territory roads, I noticed that they were not properly maintained, and many cracks could be seen here and there.
I looked around. Merchant carts and wagons were passing through while enduring those bumps.
"We have to repair this as well," I muttered and headed toward the main gate.
The closer I got, the more I understood just how impressive Blackstone Highlands must have been in its prime.
Massive stone walls stretched across the rocky cliffs, their dark surfaces blending naturally with the surrounding mountains. Time, weather, and neglect had left countless scars upon them.
Large cracks ran across several sections of the wall.
Some defensive towers had partially collapsed, their upper floors reduced to broken ruins.
Missing stones exposed gaps where repairs should have been made years ago.
Then my eyes landed on the gate itself.
Or rather—
what remained of it.
Two gigantic stone gate pillars still stood proudly on either side of the entrance.
Each pillar was nearly twenty meters tall and covered with faded carvings of swords, shields, and mountain wolves—the ancient symbols of Blackstone Highlands.
It was obvious that a magnificent gate had once stood here.
A gate capable of stopping armies.
A gate built to withstand monster hordes.
But now, the original metal gate was gone.
In its place stood a pair of thick wooden gates reinforced with iron bands.
Even those looked old and worn.
Several planks had been replaced with mismatched wood, while visible repairs covered portions of the surface.
The entire structure looked like a proud veteran desperately refusing to collapse.
Beyond the gate, steep mountain roads stretched southward through narrow valleys and rocky canyons.
Merchant caravans slowly entered and exited the territory, their wheels rattling over uneven stone roads.
Far in the distance, towering mountains pierced the clouds, while cold winds carried the scent of stone, earth, and wilderness.
Looking at the scene, I couldn’t help but imagine how prosperous this territory must have been ten years ago.
Now...
it looked like a giant slowly dying from neglect.
My gaze hardened.
"Not for much longer."
After taking one final look at the battered gate, I stepped outside.
The moment I crossed the entrance, the full view of Blackstone Highlands revealed itself before me.
I stopped for a brief moment.
From outside, the territory looked even more impressive.
Blackstone Highlands wasn’t built on flat land like most human cities.
Instead, it had been carved directly into the mountains.
Layers of stone walls, watchtowers, and buildings climbed along the rocky cliffs like giant steps ascending toward the sky.
The lord’s district sat at the highest point, overlooking everything below.
Beneath it were the residential districts, markets, barracks, and warehouses, all connected through winding roads and stairways carved into the mountain itself.
Dark gray stone structures blended naturally with the surrounding cliffs, making the territory appear like part of the mountain rather than something built upon it.
Even after years of decline, its defensive advantages were obvious.
Steep cliffs protected most sides of the settlement.
Narrow mountain paths limited the number of enemies that could advance at once.
Countless elevated positions allowed archers and mages to attack invaders from above.
A small army could easily hold back a force several times its size.
No wonder so many nobles wanted this place.
My gaze drifted farther outward.
To the north, towering peaks of the Stormhowl Mountains stretched endlessly across the horizon.
Their snow-covered summits pierced the clouds while dense forests covered their lower slopes.
Somewhere within those mountains lay the abandoned Black Iron mines and countless monster nests.
To the west, rugged hills gradually faded into distant wilderness leading toward the Demi-Human Empire.
Several old trade paths could still be seen weaving through valleys and mountain passes.
To the south, the famous Ashveil Trade Route cut across the landscape like a long brown ribbon.
Merchant caravans slowly traveled along it, their wagons appearing no larger than ants from this distance.
Beyond the road stretched vast grasslands dotted with scattered forests and rocky outcrops.
The wind blew across the highlands, carrying the scent of pine trees, fresh grass, and mountain stone.
For a moment, I simply stood there in silence.
Beautiful.
That was the first word that came to mind.
Despite the poverty.
Despite the corruption.
Despite the crumbling walls and abandoned mines.
The territory itself is breathtaking.
It possessed mountains.
Trade routes.
Natural defenses.
Valuable resources.
Everything needed to become prosperous.
The only thing it lacked... was someone capable of bringing it back to life.
A faint smile appeared on my face.
"Fortunately," I muttered.
"It has me now."
Then I turned toward the southern trade route and continued walking.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 29: The First Titan Form
paragraphs: STEP STEP STEP.
Our horse’s footsteps echoed as we sped up our journey. "Because I want to return before night."
I muttered as I looked at the passing trees and some caravans which were coming from afar.
"Elmund did say that even behind these local bandits, some nobles or organizations are involved."
I tried to count the number of caravans and wagons, but they were far away.
"Seems like everyone is forced to follow this route, which has now become beneficial to many people."
I said while gritting my teeth. "No one... literally no one can mess with my territory."
"Faster!!!"
HUFF...
"Neigh!!!"
The horses neighed as we moved faster, and just after traveling for one hour, we finally reached the location.
"Or at least the last location where those bandits were seen," I muttered as I looked around and only saw a clear marking of a clearing, which made a curved road toward the forest.
"Even though many of these bandits took toll fees and left the merchants or caravans alone, but—"
I noticed bloodstains and saw some bones in the distance.
"Sometimes greed takes over their minds."
"This way," I ordered, then we started going deeper.
"That’s why it’s all about how many mercenaries you have, because if you look too weak, then forget about your money, even keeping your life is too much of a miracle."
"Halt!"
I raised my hand, and all ten Bronze Knights stopped.
"Black Ridge Marauders."
I saw five members in cloth and leather armor patrolling with crossbows in their hands.
I looked around and found that in the distance, more than ten carts were parked, and some dead bodies were buried nearby.
"Too brutal," I thought while continuing to observe.
After a while, I finally saw the tent area, where around ten people, all of them women, were bound by ropes, and a few bandits with cleavers were guarding them.
"Spread out."
I told them, and they silently moved and slowly surrounded the whole area.
"The information is that they have around 50 Iron Knights, which is definitely way too high for a normal bandit group, then 200 Body Tempering Realm members, which seems normal though."
I said after noticing some people come out from the main tent.
Soon all of them started laughing and shouting.
I tried to hear their voices, and after focusing my aether on my ears, I was able to hear them clearly.
"Damn brother, we have hit the jackpot this time."
A bald, one-eyed bandit said as he looked toward the prisoners.
The nearby bandits laughed loudly.
"With this haul, we won’t need to rob anyone for months."
"I am buying a new sword."
"Forget a sword, I am buying a woman."
Crude laughter echoed throughout the camp.
I followed his gaze, then saw a woman who have long dark-brown hair reaching her waist and bright blue eyes.
She looked mature and have an elegant beauty.
Her clothes are high-quality travel attire mixed with light protective armor.
She and the others have wounds on their bodies.
"Seems like a fight did happen."
I noticed, but seeing the number of bandits, I knew some quality would not make up for numbers.
I continued listening.
"But brother, can’t we taste them first?"
A thin but tall black-haired bandit who has a spear on his side said with a lecherous voice to the broad-shouldered and heavily built bandit who has dark brown hair and an ugly face.
Several prisoners immediately lowered their heads.
One woman trembled visibly.
Sophia clenched her fists so tightly that blood started dripping from her palms.
"This person seems to be their leader."
I thought while noticing a massive single-edged iron greatsword beside him.
I gave the hand signal to all Bronze Knights to save the hostages while I distracted them.
"Huff!"
I took a deep breath.
Though I have Bronze Knights and they are only Iron and Body Tempering Realm members, with this many numbers we can still end up in bad shape.
I took a quick look, then shook my head.
"No need for the 2nd armor or 2nd Titan form."
"But I definitely want to try my First Titan Form."
I muttered excitedly as I stood up and started walking toward them.
STEP STEP STEP.
Soon the patrolling bandits noticed me first.
"Stop, who are you?"
One of the bandits shouted and aimed his crossbow at me.
WHOOSHH.
As I didn’t reply, he released the bolt.
CRACK.
As he released the arrow, I caught it easily with my hand and crushed it.
Their faces changed instantly.
"W-What?"
"He caught it?"
The five patrolling bandits subconsciously took a step back.

The bandits in the center of the campfire also noticed the commotion and each picked up their weapons and started moving toward me, though the leader and the two close to him didn’t take me seriously.
"Nyx Ascension."
I said in a normal voice.
BOOM.
A heavy pressure exploded from my body as the surrounding leaves and dirt were blown away.
Trees started shaking from the pressure, and the five patrolling bandits instantly backed away.
The camp suddenly fell silent.
My height slowly grew.
As my clothes ripped apart.
Seven feet.
Eight.
Nine.
And finally it stopped at ten feet.
My whole body is bound by blue-black chains, and the ends of them stretched back into the Void.
Now even their main leaders stand up because they could sense danger.
The prisoners also look toward me with hope in their eyes.
One woman whispered.
"A knight..."
Another silently began praying.
[Luke, those chains are stopping you from summoning and unlocking your Titan Form.]
I narrowed my eyes as I heard the System’s irritated voice.
"Then what should I do?"
I asked while the bandits started surrounding me.
[Use your ancient ritual words and summon it with your full willpower.]
I heard the System’s explanation, then took a deep breath and closed my eyes for a second.
The bandits and their leaders narrowed their eyes.
"Did he get afraid?"
One of them asked, as if it didn’t matter that the person before him is ten feet tall.
The leader’s expression has already become serious.
His instincts are screaming at him.
Danger.
Extreme danger.
My eyes opened as I called my armor.
"Descend, Velzareth."
Soon a black armor materialized from the Void behind me with azure-blue runes covering it.
CLACK-CLICK.
It attached itself to my body and fit perfectly without a helmet.
Then I raised Voidfang toward the dark sky.
The surrounding bandits unconsciously took several steps back.
Even bandit leader expression became serious.
The forest fell silent.
No insects.
No birds.
No wind.
As if the world itself is listening.
Then I spoke.
"From the darkness beyond the world’s edge..."
RUMBLE.
The sky trembled.
Dark clouds gathered from every direction.
The stars vanished one by one behind an unnatural darkness.
A cold chill spread through the entire forest.
Several horses panicked and collapsed to their knees.
"W-What is happening?"
One of the bandits stumbled backward.
"Chains that bind the forgotten one..."
CLANG.
CLANG.
CLANG.
Massive blue-black chains wrapped around my body suddenly became visible.
Countless runes ignited across their surface.
The chains stretched endlessly behind me into a black void that had appeared in the sky.
As if they were connected to something far beyond this world.
The prisoners stared with widened eyes.
Several bandits instinctively lowered their weapons.
Even bandit leader’s grip tightened around his Blacktooth Cleaver.
Far beyond reality.
Beyond stars.
Beyond time.
Beyond the edge of existence itself.
Thirteen colossal Titans remained crucified within an endless void.
Each one large enough to dwarf worlds.
Ancient chains pierced their flesh.
Ancient armor sealed their bodies.
All of them remain as motionless, silent and forgotten.
Then my voice reached them.
"Shatter."
CRACK.
A single crack appeared upon the chains binding the dark-blue-haired Titan.
The sound echoed through eternity.
CRACK.
CRACK.
CRACK.
More fractures spread.
The Titan slowly raised his head.
For the first time in countless ages.
His eyes opened.
Within those eyes—
Entire galaxies were born and destroyed.
Back in the forest—
Everyone froze.
The pressure descending from the sky multiplied instantly.
BOOOOOM.
Trees bent.
Leaves exploded outward.
Several weaker bandits collapsed to their knees.
Blood trickled from their noses.
"W-What monster is this?!"
One of them screamed.
"Awaken..."
The Titan moved.
Only slightly.
But that tiny movement caused the void itself to tremble.
The chains tightened violently.
Trying to suppress him.
Trying to drag him back into eternal imprisonment.
The Titan opened his mouth.
And released a silent roar.
A roar so ancient that even the sound doesn’t understand it.
"Nyx Titan."
ROOOOOOOOOOOOAR.
The silent roar finally reached reality.
The sky shattered like glass.
Darkness swallowed the heavens.
Azure-blue lightning erupted across the clouds.
The void behind me expanded.
Everyone instinctively looked upward.
Their faces pale.
Their bodies trembling.
Even bandit leader took a step backward.
For the first time in years.
He felt fear.
True fear.
"Warden of the Void Path."
SHATTER.
SHATTER.
SHATTER.
The chains exploded.
One after another.
Across the void.
Across reality.
Across my body.
Fragments of blue-black chains scattered like dying stars.
The imprisoned Titan stood.
Free.
At last.
For a brief moment—
the entire world saw him.
A primordial hunter.
An ancient executioner.
A being born from the darkness beyond the world’s edge.
Then his body dissolved into countless particles of blue-black light.
And surged toward me.
WHOOSSSSH.
The light entered my body.
My height increased again.
Ten feet.
Eleven.
Twelve.
My physique became lean and predatory.
Long dark-blue hair flowed behind me.
Azure eyes burned like twin stars.
Black-blue runes spread across my skin and armor.
Void energy leaked from every breath.
Silence descended.
No one dared to move.
No one dared to speak.
Even the forest seemed afraid.
I slowly opened my eyes.
The world has become prey.
A faint smile appeared on my face.
"Freedom."
Far beyond mortal lands.
Beyond kingdoms.
Beyond worlds.
Several ancient eyes suddenly opened.
Some belonged to forgotten gods.
Some to beings older than history itself.
Their gazes pierced countless realms before locking onto the same source.
Silence followed.
Then—
"...A being from the Forgotten Era?" an ancient voice whispered.
Impossible.
The age of Titans had ended long ago.
A golden-eyed god slowly rose from his throne.
His expression darkened.
"Something has awakened."
Across another distant realm, an ancient existence wrapped in endless stars opened its eyes.
For the first time in countless years—
surprise appeared on its face.
"The Warden of the Void Path..."
Then the connection vanished.
As though whatever had awakened refused to be observed.
And for the first time in ages—
Fear stirred within the hearts of beings who once believed themselves eternal.
[Chapter End]

"Chains that bind the forgotten one..."
CLANG.
CLANG.
CLANG.
Massive blue-black chains wrapped around my body suddenly became visible.
Countless runes ignited across their surface.
The chains stretched endlessly behind me into a black void that had appeared in the sky.
As if they were connected to something far beyond this world.
The prisoners stared with widened eyes.
Several bandits instinctively lowered their weapons.
Even bandit leader’s grip tightened around his Blacktooth Cleaver.
Far beyond reality.
Beyond stars.
Beyond time.
Beyond the edge of existence itself.
Thirteen colossal Titans remained crucified within an endless void.
Each one large enough to dwarf worlds.
Ancient chains pierced their flesh.
Ancient armor sealed their bodies.
All of them remain as motionless, silent and forgotten.
Then my voice reached them.
"Shatter."
CRACK.
A single crack appeared upon the chains binding the dark-blue-haired Titan.
The sound echoed through eternity.
CRACK.
CRACK.
CRACK.
More fractures spread.
The Titan slowly raised his head.
For the first time in countless ages.
His eyes opened.
Within those eyes—
Entire galaxies were born and destroyed.
Back in the forest—
Everyone froze.
The pressure descending from the sky multiplied instantly.
BOOOOOM.
Trees bent.
Leaves exploded outward.
Several weaker bandits collapsed to their knees.
Blood trickled from their noses.
"W-What monster is this?!"
One of them screamed.
"Awaken..."
The Titan moved.
Only slightly.
But that tiny movement caused the void itself to tremble.
The chains tightened violently.
Trying to suppress him.
Trying to drag him back into eternal imprisonment.
The Titan opened his mouth.
And released a silent roar.
A roar so ancient that even the sound doesn’t understand it.
"Nyx Titan."
ROOOOOOOOOOOOAR.
The silent roar finally reached reality.
The sky shattered like glass.
Darkness swallowed the heavens.
Azure-blue lightning erupted across the clouds.
The void behind me expanded.
Everyone instinctively looked upward.
Their faces pale.
Their bodies trembling.
Even bandit leader took a step backward.
For the first time in years.
He felt fear.
True fear.
"Warden of the Void Path."
SHATTER.
SHATTER.
SHATTER.
The chains exploded.
One after another.
Across the void.
Across reality.
Across my body.
Fragments of blue-black chains scattered like dying stars.
The imprisoned Titan stood.
Free.
At last.
For a brief moment—
the entire world saw him.
A primordial hunter.
An ancient executioner.
A being born from the darkness beyond the world’s edge.
Then his body dissolved into countless particles of blue-black light.
And surged toward me.
WHOOSSSSH.
The light entered my body.
My height increased again.
Ten feet.
Eleven.
Twelve.
My physique became lean and predatory.
Long dark-blue hair flowed behind me.
Azure eyes burned like twin stars.
Black-blue runes spread across my skin and armor.
Void energy leaked from every breath.
Silence descended.
No one dared to move.
No one dared to speak.
Even the forest seemed afraid.
I slowly opened my eyes.
The world has become prey.
A faint smile appeared on my face.
"Freedom."
Far beyond mortal lands.
Beyond kingdoms.
Beyond worlds.
Several ancient eyes suddenly opened.
Some belonged to forgotten gods.
Some to beings older than history itself.
Their gazes pierced countless realms before locking onto the same source.
Silence followed.
Then—
"...A being from the Forgotten Era?" an ancient voice whispered.
Impossible.
The age of Titans had ended long ago.
A golden-eyed god slowly rose from his throne.
His expression darkened.
"Something has awakened."
Across another distant realm, an ancient existence wrapped in endless stars opened its eyes.
For the first time in countless years—
surprise appeared on its face.
"The Warden of the Void Path..."
Then the connection vanished.
As though whatever had awakened refused to be observed.
And for the first time in ages—
Fear stirred within the hearts of beings who once believed themselves eternal.
[Chapter End]

chapters.title: Chapter 30: Born from Darkness
paragraphs: "Wake up!!!" The muscular bandit leader shouted toward everyone with an angry voice.

All the bandits that were trembling suddenly stopped somewhat and awoke from their fear. They turned to look at their leader, whose Peak Iron Knight aura was fully released as his body was slightly covered with a thin layer of black-silver colored aether.
"Who cares if he becomes huge?" he yelled while moving toward me with his two strongest fighters, the one-eyed bald bandit and the other thin bandit with long black hair holding a spear.
I tilted my head, amused by their confidence.
The leader completely ignored this as he continued, "He is alone, and that’s all that matters."
The other bandits finally relaxed somewhat and laughed, trying to calm down their trembling hands as they increased their grip on their swords.
"Hahaha, yeah! He is alone and we have hundreds!!!"
The other bandits also started shouting at this.
The female prisoners looked worriedly toward my side, but—
"HAHAHAHA!"
I laughed loudly with one hand holding my face, as all of this was very funny.
As my laugh echoed, their expressions changed slightly as they looked toward me with questions in their heads.
"Did he finally lose it?"
They gave each other careful glances and started approaching me.

While they were moving, my Bronze Knights also slowly started closing the distance from the prisoners, as most of the bandits’ attention was focused on me, so only a few bandits remained there, even though they were also looking toward me.
"Alone?"
Suddenly my mocking voice came out from behind my hand-covered face, but they could see my lips, which had now turned into a smile.
SHIVER.
All of them shivered from this, as even the leader found something suspicious.
"Archers and Crossbowmen, aim your weapons!"
He shouted hurriedly toward everyone who were ranged fighters.
"Yes!"
More than a hundred bandits got startled by the sudden order, but they obliged and hastily loaded their bolts and arrows. Then each of them from a distance aimed their ranged weapons toward me.
Though I could see some were aiming while hiding behind trees or stones.
I ignored their futile bravery and instead looked toward my Nyx Titan ability.
[Nyx Titan: Racial Ability]
| Shadow of Nyx |
Description:
The signature ability of the Nyx Titan.
The user summons a Void Doppelganger born from the darkness of the Void Path.
Unlike ordinary illusions, the Shadow of Nyx is a real combat entity capable of fighting alongside its master.
The shadow possesses the user’s current physical strength and can independently engage enemies.
As a primordial hunting technique of the Nyx Titans, this ability was once used to overwhelm prey from multiple directions before delivering the final execution.
"Crazy."
I muttered after reading its description, then lowered my hand slowly, but the next moment—
Dark blue and black Void Energy gathered beside me.
It became darkness.
Then it twisted.
A second figure slowly emerged.
It had the same face and same eyes as me.
Its presence also felt similar, so identical that hardly anyone could tell the difference.
But there was one difference.
Its body appeared darker.
Then—
The Shadow opened its eyes.
FLINCH.
Everyone took a step back after seeing this bizarre thing born from the darkness, but it felt even more wrong when it looked the same as that laughing giant.
"What the hell is this?"
The archers’ and crossbowmen’s hands trembled and their weapons lowered slightly after seeing this, but the next moment their pupils widened so much that if someone said run, they would do it.
Because another shadow appeared beside both giants.
Now a total of four smiling giants were standing together, and each gave off the same suffocating pressure.
"Idiots, what are you waiting for? Fire!!!"
Suddenly all of them heard their leader’s furious voice.
Then they came out of their fear and without hesitating anymore all released their arrows and bolts.
WHOOSSHH.
I watched calmly at the incoming volleys of arrows and the expression of the bandit leader who was thinking I was already dead.
"Go."
The next moment everyone heard my calm voice, as the three shadows took a step in front of me and then each of them raised their large longswords.
"Voidfang."
They muttered slowly, then started rotating the swords with one hand.
CRACK. CRASH. SHATTER.
Everyone’s face became ugly as all the arrows shattered or were deflected after colliding with the rotating swords.
But the next moment, as the volleys of arrows stopped, the three giants suddenly disappeared and everyone heard a loud sound of the ground shattering.
BOOM!
"What!!!"
All of them exclaimed, but soon they found the answer as twenty bandits in the front were cut in half cleanly by three large black longswords.
SLASH.
"Nice."
The word escaped my mouth after witnessing this slash, then my gaze turned toward the remaining system information.
• Possesses 100% of Luke’s current physical strength
• Can fight independently
• Shares combat instincts with the user
• Can use Nyx Titan abilities
• Can equip and use Velzareth
• Can wield Voidfang
• Remains active while stamina is supplied.
"Yup! They also have the ability to summon doppelgangers."
I said in a normal tone, but sadly.
Current Limitation:
• High stamina consumption
• Long battles rapidly drain the user
"When I was a Body Tempering Realm user, I could only summon one shadow because I couldn’t bear the stamina consumption for more."
Then I looked toward the three shadow giants who were thrashing and killing enemies like children.
The archers hastily loaded their weapons before firing again at them, but each of them just jumped too high, as all the arrows passed them without doing any damage.
But next came their nightmare.
BOOM. BOOM. BOOM.
Three explosions occurred as each shadow giant dropped from the sky with their full strength.
"That’s why they were erased, because if I had unlimited stamina, I could become a one-man army."
I said, but—
"I can summon only three shadow giants in the Iron Knight Realm."
I muttered sadly, then turned my gaze toward the prisoners and they were gone.
"Good."
I smiled that my Bronze Knights had finally done their work after seeing some bandit bodies scattered around the prisoner area.
The bandit leader’s face also changed after he looked back toward the corpses and understood that all of this was just a distraction.
But I didn’t give him a chance to think more as I threw my Voidfang sword directly at him.
WHOOSH.
"Don’t underestimate me!"
The bandit leader returned to his senses, then shouted as his muscles bulged and his eyes became bloodshot.
Then he struck back with his large great cleaver in an attempt to knock back Voidfang, which was now eight feet long.
BOOOOM! CRASHH!
Sadly, he overestimated himself and got blown away along with his sword-holding right hand.
"Well, my aura still belongs to the Early Iron Knight Realm."
I shook my head.
If my first armor bonus strength had not been removed and my First Titan Form strength now only increased my strength by one time, his body would have been blown apart by the previous attack.
BANG!
After taking one step, I charged toward him and killed every enemy with one punch that came along the way.
Sophia watched all this carnage with her bright blue eyes from the distance, in which there was not a single bit of sympathy for them.
Because they killed all of her subordinates and assaulted many women as well.
"If not for my status, then my outcome would not be any better."
She shook her head to remove those memories.
"Who is that person?"
She turned toward her saviors, knights in black-silver colored armor who were distributing food and water to the other women that were saved.
All the women were crying because they had faced many things, and some even had resentment toward their leader.
"Why did only we suffer so much? But she’s fine."
They thought when they looked at her clean appearance.
Sophia also noticed some women had a different attitude toward her, but she didn’t care about this.
The Bronze Knights stopped and told her about their master.
[Chapter End]
